paras.en: The Turtle Island organization in Graz, Austria — which recently started breeding the turtles in Austria as a "genetic reservoir for eventual rewilding" and is working to help preserve them in Mexico — considers it "the world's smallest turtle species," and estimates that "over 99%" of its natural habitat has been lost to urbanization.
paras.zh: 奥地利格拉茨的海龟岛组织最近开始在奥地利繁殖海龟，作为“最终野化的遗传库”，并正在努力帮助墨西哥保护它们。该组织认为海龟是“世界上最小的海龟物种”，并估计“超过 99%”的自然栖息地已因城市化而消失。

paras.en: Roads and traffic are a particular risk for the slow-moving creatures.
paras.zh: 对于行动缓慢的生物来说，道路和交通是一个特别的风险。

paras.en: "Despite strict protections, their small size and striking appearance make them prime targets for illegal collectors," Turtle Island says when detailing other risks to the tiny animals, that are not known to grow larger than 10 centimeters (less than 4 inches) in length.
paras.zh: 海龟岛在详细介绍这种小型动物面临的其他风险时表示：“尽管受到严格的保护，但它们的小​​尺寸和引人注目的外观使它们成为非法收集者的主要目标。”据了解，这些小型动物的长度不会超过 10 厘米（不到 4 英寸）。

paras.en: The IUCN Red List classifies it as "Critically Endangered" and it is subject to the highest level of protection under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).
paras.zh: 世界自然保护联盟红色名录将其列为“极度濒危”，并受到《濒危野生动植物种国际贸易公约》（CITES）的最高级别保护。

paras.en: "The suspected poaching of 26 of these turtles from the wild may have reduced the population by nearly 10%," the NVWA wrote, basing its figure on the estimated population of around 300 of the turtles in the wild.
paras.zh: NVWA 写道：“涉嫌从野外偷猎 26 只海龟，可能导致其数量减少近 10%。”这一数字是根据野生海龟约 300 只的估计数量得出的。

paras.en: The agency urged people to report any suspected instances of illegal trade of protected animal or plant species, whether "via online forums, marketplaces, bird fairs, or antique and curiosity markets."
paras.zh: 该机构敦促人们举报任何可疑的受保护动物或植物物种非法贸易案件，无论是“通过在线论坛、市场、鸟类集市还是古董和古玩市场”。

articles.title: Divisions deepen between EU member states after tense budget summit

paras.en: EU leaders arrived in Brussels braced for a difficult showdown over the bloc's multitrillion-euro seven-year budget. But few expected the summit to unravel so quickly, with talks breaking down late on Thursday night.
paras.zh: 欧盟领导人抵达布鲁塞尔，准备就欧盟数万亿欧元的七年预算进行艰难的摊牌。但很少有人预料到峰会会如此迅速地破裂，会谈于周四深夜破裂。

paras.en: Squabbles and thinly veiled public barbs meant they left without a deal and didn't even attempt to resume discussions on the planned second day.
paras.zh: 争吵和几乎不加掩饰的公开倒刺意味着他们在没有达成协议的情况下离开，甚至没有试图在计划的第二天恢复讨论。

paras.en: There is a self-imposed deadline to find agreement before the end of 2026 on the budget which covers the 2028-2034 period. But experts say there is no cause for alarm, yet.
paras.zh: 双方自行设定了在 2026 年底之前就 2028-2034 年预算达成一致的最后期限。但专家表示，目前还没有理由惊慌。

paras.en: "Every time there are long-term EU budget negotiations, there are breakdowns, chaos, recrimination and a lot of political theater and drama," said Jacob Funk Kirkegaard, an EU economist and expert at the Bruegel think tank in Brussels.
paras.zh: 布鲁塞尔布鲁盖尔智库的欧盟经济学家、专家雅各布·芬克·柯克加德表示：“每次欧盟长期预算谈判都会出现破裂、混乱、相互指责以及大量政治戏剧。”

paras.en: The center of that political theater this time was the prime ministers of Denmark, Sweden, Belgium and Austria — countries wanting a reduced budget — who staged a walkout during smaller, group meetings, claiming the atmosphere had not been constructive to getting a deal.
paras.zh: 这次政治舞台的中心是丹麦、瑞典、比利时和奥地利等希望削减预算的国家的总理，他们在较小的小组会议期间举行了罢工，声称气氛不利于达成协议。

paras.en: Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar called the whole summit "completely unnecessary," pointing the blame at the man who had decided to call it and whose job it is to meditate the talks, European Council President Antonio Costa.
paras.zh: 匈牙利总理彼得·马扎尔 (Peter Magyar) 称整个峰会“完全没有必要”，并将责任归咎于决定召开这次峰会、负责酝酿此次会谈的欧洲理事会主席安东尼奥·科斯塔 (Antonio Costa)。

paras.en: Costa was diplomatic in defending his decision to bring the leaders to Brussels, telling the press: "For me it was very useful to figure out the parameters of a possible landing zone in December."
paras.zh: 科斯塔为自己将领导人带到布鲁塞尔的决定进行了外交辩护，他对媒体表示：“对我来说，弄清楚 12 月份可能登陆区的参数非常有用。”

paras.en: Germany demands more for competitiveness, security, defense
paras.zh: 德国对竞争力、安全和国防提出更多要求

paras.en: Long before the summit started, Germany had laid down an ultimatum — Berlin would only sign off on the budget if all the other EU countries greenlit an additional €45 billion ($49 billion) support loan for Ukraine to fund the country in its war efforts through 2027.
paras.zh: 早在峰会开始之前，德国就下了最后通牒——只有所有其他欧盟国家都批准向乌克兰提供额外的 450 亿欧元（合 490 亿美元）支持贷款，以资助该国到 2027 年的战争努力，柏林才会签署预算。

paras.en: Hungary, Czechia, Bulgaria and Slovakia have dug their heels in against the proposal, insisting that giving Ukraine money to buy weapons will prolong the war. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico even accused Germany of "blackmail."
paras.zh: 匈牙利、捷克、保加利亚和斯洛伐克坚决反对这一提议，坚称向乌克兰提供资金购买武器将延长战争。斯洛伐克总理罗伯特·菲科甚至指责德国“敲诈勒索”。

paras.en: As Europe's biggest economy, Germany's contribution amounts to around 25% of the whole budget.
paras.zh: 作为欧洲最大的经济体，德国的捐款约占整个预算的25%。

paras.en: In a press conference after the summit, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said "hundreds of billions" still need to be slashed. The European Commission's original proposal of approximately €1.786 trillion had already been reduced by €204 billion (down 10.2%).
paras.zh: 德国总理弗里德里希·梅尔茨在峰会后的新闻发布会上表示，仍需削减“数千亿美元”。欧盟委员会最初提议的约1.786万亿欧元已减少2040亿欧元（下降10.2%）。

paras.en: "Europe needs to exercise a sense of proportion," said Merz. "The budget cannot grow indefinitely, and the burden of financing it must be distributed fairly."
paras.zh: 默茨说：“欧洲需要保持分寸感。” “预算不能无限期增长，融资负担必须公平分配。”

paras.en: Merz also aimed a comment toward Costa, who has been renewing the details in the budget proposal at every stage.
paras.zh: 默茨还针对科斯塔发表了评论，科斯塔在每个阶段都在更新预算提案中的细节。

paras.en: "The proposals that have been on the table so far are not a basis for an agreement," said Merz.
paras.zh: 默茨表示：“迄今为止摆在桌面上的提案并不是达成协议的基础。”

paras.en: Costa did tell leaders on Thursday that he is planning to cut between €220 billion to €230 billion out of the next proposal.
paras.zh: 科斯塔周四确实告诉领导人，他计划从下一个提案中削减 2200 亿至 2300 亿欧元。

paras.en: Berlin's budget reduction push is backed by six other countries who together call themselves the "Sensible Seven." All pay more into the collective EU financial pot than they receive out of it.
paras.zh: 柏林的预算削减举措得到了其他六个国家的支持，这些国家统称为“明智七国”。所有国家向欧盟集体财政支出的投入都超过了他们从中获得的收入。

paras.en: They are opposed by 17 EU member states who insist the total budget should grow, led by France and Italy. These countries call themselves the "Friends of Cohesion" — a nod to the EU cohesion funds which are used to share wealth from the EU's richer regions and nations to its poorer ones.
paras.zh: 他们遭到以法国和意大利为首的 17 个欧盟成员国的反对，这些国家坚持认为总预算应该增长。这些国家称自己为“凝聚力之友”——这是对欧盟凝聚力基金的认可，该基金用于将欧盟较富裕地区和国家的财富分享给较贫穷的地区和国家。

paras.en: In the current proposal, agriculture, fisheries and cohesion spending falls from 59.1% to 42.4%, while money for economic competitiveness, security, and defense rises from 17.7% to 27.7%. This rebalancing is a key German demand.
paras.zh: 在当前提案中，农业、渔业和凝聚力支出从 59.1% 下降至 42.4%，而用于经济竞争力、安全和国防的资金从 17.7% 上升至 27.7%。这种再平衡是德国的一个关键需求。

paras.en: The EU is also searching for a way to add money into the budget that doesn't come from national contributions. The current proposal includes a controversial EU-wide digital tax which could chart a course for a major battle with the US.
paras.zh: 欧盟还在寻找一种方法，将非国家捐款的资金添加到预算中。目前的提案包括一项有争议的欧盟范围内的数字税，这可能为与美国的重大斗争指明方向。

paras.en: The idea, originally put forward by French President Emmanuel Macron, is for a 3% tax on revenues of online advertising, online marketplaces and on the monetization of user data. The money, to be paid directly into the EU's budget, is estimated to bring in €5 billion per year.
paras.zh: 该想法最初由法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙 (Emmanuel Macron) 提出，即对在线广告、在线市场和用户数据货币化的收入征收 3% 的税。这笔钱将直接支付给欧盟预算，预计每年可带来 50 亿欧元的收入。

paras.en: But the proposal is ringing alarm bells in Ireland, where US tech giants like Google, Meta, Apple, Microsoft and LinkedIn have their European headquarters.
paras.zh: 但这一提议给爱尔兰敲响了警钟，谷歌、Meta、苹果、微软和 LinkedIn 等美国科技巨头的欧洲总部都设在爱尔兰。

paras.en: "A digital tax is sending out all the wrong messages," said Irish Prime Minister Micheal Martin, who could still veto the proposal.
paras.zh: 爱尔兰总理迈克尔·马丁表示：“数字税正在发出错误的信息。”他仍然可以否决该提案。

paras.en: There is a fear in some European capitals that without being able to generate its own funds, future EU loans could downgrade the European Commission's unblemished standing on international markets.
paras.zh: 一些欧洲国家首都担心，如果无法产生自己的资金，未来的欧盟贷款可能会降低欧盟委员会在国际市场上完美的地位。

paras.en: The EU has around €860 billion in outstanding debts it took out for its pandemic recovery funding and to support Ukraine. Its triple-A credit rating could be downgraded if Marine Le Pen, the far-right front-runner in France's presidential election, wins in the spring and follows through on her promise to reduce French contributions to the EU budget.
paras.zh: 欧盟有约 8600 亿欧元的未偿债务，用于为疫情复苏提供资金并支持乌克兰。如果法国总统选举中极右翼领先者马琳·勒庞(Marine Le Pen)在春季获胜并兑现减少法国对欧盟预算捐款的承诺，其AAA信用评级可能会被下调。

paras.en: EU member states that favor a financing model through national contributions rather than through tax revenue "understand very well what will happen if the EU loses its triple-A rating," said Bruegel's Kirkegaard. "Interest rate costs will go up even more. Who has to pay for that? Net contributing countries, like Germany, the Nordics, the Dutch, which is why they are much more open to this than in the past."
paras.zh: 布鲁盖尔的柯克加德表示，赞成通过国家缴款而非税收收入融资模式的欧盟成员国“非常清楚，如果欧盟失去 3A 评级将会发生什么”。 “利率成本将进一步上升。谁必须为此买单？净贡献国，如德国、北欧、荷兰，这就是为什么他们对此比过去更加开放。”

paras.en: Other European tax experts believe that prior examples of these digital taxes show the costs outweigh the benefits.
paras.zh: 其他欧洲税务专家认为，这些数字税的先前例子表明成本大于收益。

paras.en: "We analyzed the states which have a digital services tax [DST], and we've seen that economic cost exceeds the revenue generated," said Cristina Enache, an economist at the Brussels-based nonprofit Tax Foundation Europe. "Spain has a DST and the expected revenue was twice or three times larger than what they actually are collecting."
paras.zh: “我们分析了征收数字服务税 [DST] 的州，我们发现经济成本超过了产生的收入，”总部位于布鲁塞尔的非营利性欧洲税收基金会的经济学家 Cristina Enache 表示。 “西班牙实行夏令时，预期收入比实际收入高出两到三倍。”

paras.en: Enache called the tax proposal "politically impossible."
paras.zh: 埃纳什称这项税收提案“在政治上是不可能的”。

paras.en: EU leaders know that the clock on their end-of-2026 deadline is ticking, and will return to the same conference rooms in late December hoping for a more conducive atmosphere to strike a deal.
paras.zh: 欧盟领导人知道 2026 年底的最后期限已经过去，他们将在 12 月底回到同一会议室，希望营造一个更有利于达成协议的氛围。

articles.title: Canada: Supreme Court largely upholds Quebec secularism bill

paras.en: Canada's Supreme Court on Friday upheld Quebec's ban on religious symbols for public servants.
paras.zh: 加拿大最高法院周五维持魁北克省禁止公务员佩戴宗教标志的禁令。

paras.en: However, it ruled that provincial lawmakers should be allowed to wear religious symbols in the legislature, Quebec's National Assembly.
paras.zh: 然而，它规定省级立法者应该被允许在魁北克国民议会的立法机构中佩戴宗教标志。

paras.en: Quebec's government passed the bill, known as Bill 21, in 2019, arguing it was necessary to protect its secular society.
paras.zh: 魁北克政府于 2019 年通过了这项名为第 21 号法案的法案，认为有必要保护其世俗社会。

paras.en: Under the law, anyone receiving public services like teachers and police officers has the right to do so without being exposed to overt religious symbols, including hijabs, turbans and yarmulkes.
paras.zh: 根据法律，任何接受公共服务的人，如教师和警察，都有权这样做，而不必接触公开的宗教象征，包括头巾、头巾和圆顶小帽。

paras.en: What did the Supreme Court say about the law?
paras.zh: 最高法院对该法律有何评论？

paras.en: Chief Justice Richard Wagner said that the law "is rooted in Quebec's legitimate and historical commitment to ensuring the (secularism) of the state in a free and democratic society."
paras.zh: 首席大法官理查德·瓦格纳表示，该法律“植根于魁北克对确保国家在自由民主社会中的（世俗主义）的合法和历史承诺。”

paras.en: Mathieu Levesque, the interim the right-wing Quebecois nationalist Future Quebec Coalition (CAQ) that passed the bill, hailed it as a "victory" for the French-speaking province.
paras.zh: 通过该法案的右翼魁北克民族主义者未来魁北克联盟（CAQ）的临时代表马蒂厄·莱维斯克（Mathieu Levesque）称赞该法案是法语省份的“胜利”。

paras.en: "This is a victory for the Quebec nation and for [CAQ], whose actions have today been fully validated," he said.
paras.zh: “这是魁北克国家和 [CAQ] 的胜利，他们的行动今天已得到充分验证，”他说。

paras.en: CAQ ruled Quebec in two parliamentary terms from 2018 to 2026, after which it failed to enter parliament and the pro-independence center-left Parti Quebecois (PQ), which also supported Bill 21, formed government.
paras.zh: CAQ在2018年至2026年期间经历了两届议会任期，之后未能进入议会，支持独立的中左翼魁北克党（PQ）也支持第21号法案，组建了政府。

paras.en: The case was seen as a major test of how far provinces can go in defying provisions of the federal constitution by invoking the "notwithstanding clause," which effectively allows provincial governments to pass laws that may breach Canada's constitution.
paras.zh: 此案被视为对各省在多大程度上可以通过援引“尽管条款”来藐视联邦宪法条款的重大考验，该条款实际上允许省政府通过可能违反加拿大宪法的法律。

paras.en: Quebec invoked the clause when passing the secularism bill, known as Bill 21, expecting it to be challenged over constitutional provisions guaranteeing freedom of religion.
paras.zh: 魁北克省在通过世俗主义法案（即第 21 号法案）时援引了该条款，预计该法案会因保障宗教自由的宪法条款而受到挑战。

paras.en: Critics argue secularism bill weakens rights protections
paras.zh: 批评者认为世俗主义法案削弱了权利保护

paras.en: Critics have argued that the bill unfairly targets Muslim women and weakens legal protections for fundamental rights.
paras.zh: 批评人士认为，该法案不公平地针对穆斯林女性，并削弱了对基本权利的法律保护。

paras.en: "This decision is an unrestricted license for every government in this country to pass legislation taking away the fundamental freedoms and the legal rights of every Canadian ," Stephen Brown, CEO of the National Council of Canadian Muslims, was cited by Reuters news agency as saying.
paras.zh: 路透社援引加拿大穆斯林全国委员会首席执行官斯蒂芬·布朗的话说：“这一决定是对这个国家每个政府通过立法剥夺每个加拿大人的基本自由和合法权利的无限制许可。”

paras.en: He said the law forced many Muslim women to stop working as teachers or even prevented them from volunteering in schools.
paras.zh: 他说，该法律迫使许多穆斯林女性停止从事教师工作，甚至阻止她们在学校从事志愿工作。

paras.en: Emmett Macfarlane, head of political science at the University of Waterloo, was cited by Reuters as saying that the law amounted to "Islamophobia as a state policy."
paras.zh: 路透社援引滑铁卢大学政治学系主任埃米特·麦克法兰的话说，该法律相当于“仇视伊斯兰作为一项国家政策”。

articles.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secrets as AI race heats up

paras.en: OpenAI has sued Apple, accusing the Big Tech giant of stealing its trade secrets and blocking its access to hardware suppliers after Apple sued OpenAI for allegedly poaching its employees to gain access to its technology.
paras.zh: OpenAI 起诉苹果，指控这家大型科技巨头窃取其商业机密，并在苹果起诉 OpenAI 涉嫌挖走其员工以获得其技术后阻止其与硬件供应商的接触。

paras.en: The ChatGPT maker filed counterclaims in California federal court on Friday, saying that Apple’s employment practices were designed to “trap” employees and prevent them from working on competitors’ technology.
paras.zh: ChatGPT 制造商周五向加州联邦法院提起反诉，称苹果的雇佣做法旨在“困住”员工，阻止他们从事竞争对手的技术工作。

paras.en: Apple and OpenAI did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.
paras.zh: 苹果和 OpenAI 没有立即回应路透社的置评请求。

paras.en: Tensions between the two tech companies have escalated as the intensifying race to develop AI products fuels competition for talent and proprietary technology.
paras.zh: 随着开发人工智能产品的激烈竞争加剧了人才和专有技术的竞争，两家科技公司之间的紧张关系不断升级。

paras.en: In July, Apple sued OpenAI and two former employees, alleging misappropriation of its trade secrets to benefit the ChatGPT owner’s foray into consumer hardware. OpenAI has denied those allegations.
paras.zh: 7 月，苹果起诉 OpenAI 和两名前员工，指控其盗用其商业机密，以利于 ChatGPT 所有者进军消费硬件领域。 OpenAI 否认了这些指控。

paras.en: The litigation sets up a battle over who will control future AI devices that may not use traditional apps or operating systems — devices which, if successful, would direct consumer attention away from Apple’s best-selling iPhone. Analysts believe OpenAI is working on a phone or other device of its own.
paras.zh: 该诉讼引发了一场关于谁将控制未来可能不使用传统应用程序或操作系统的人工智能设备的斗争，这些设备如果成功，将引导消费者将注意力从苹果最畅销的 iPhone 上转移开。分析师认为 OpenAI 正在开发自己的手机或其他设备。

articles.title: Venezuela to repeal law that bans opposition figures from office

paras.en: Venezuela will repeal a law that prohibits opposition figures from office, National Assembly Chief Jorge Rodriguez has announced.
paras.zh: 国民议会议长豪尔赫·罗德里格斯宣布，委内瑞拉将废除一项禁止反对派人士任职的法律。

paras.en: The legislation, approved in 2024 and criticised for enabling political persecution, targeted those who promoted or supported sanctions against the country.
paras.zh: 该立法于 2024 年获得批准，并因助长政治迫害而受到批评，该立法针对的是那些推动或支持对该国实施制裁的人。

paras.en: “That law responded to a very specific moment in a particular situation that Venezuela was going through,” Rodriguez said on Thursday.
paras.zh: 罗德里格斯周四表示：“该法律针对的是委内瑞拉正在经历的特定情况下的一个非常具体的时刻。”

paras.en: The law was passed just after fraught elections which the then-incumbent Nicolas Maduro ultimately won amid widespread allegations of fraud.
paras.zh: 该法律是在充满争议的选举后不久通过的，时任总统尼古拉斯·马杜罗最终在广泛的欺诈指控中获胜。

paras.en: An interim government headed by Delcy Rodriguez, the parliamentary chief’s sister, has run Venezuela since Maduro’s abduction by US forces in January. Delcy Rodriguez promised in September during a speech at the United Nations that the South American country will hold free and fair elections, without setting a date.
paras.zh: 自马杜罗一月份被美军绑架以来，由议会主席的妹妹德尔西·罗德里格斯领导的临时政府一直在管理委内瑞拉。德尔西·罗德里格斯九月在联合国演讲时承诺，这个南美国家将举行自由公正的选举，但没有确定日期。

paras.en: Since then, the US-backed government has been in political transition talks with parts of the opposition selected by Washington. That dialogue had reached an agreement to review several laws, including the one up for repeal now, according to Jorge Rodriguez.
paras.zh: 此后，美国支持的政府一直与华盛顿选定的部分反对派进行政治过渡谈判。豪尔赫·罗德里格斯表示，这次对话达成了一项协议，将审查几项法律，其中包括现在准备废除的一项法律。

paras.en: Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado shook up Venezuelan politics with her surprise return from exile last month. Machado won an opposition primary in 2023 to take on Maduro in the following year’s election, but she was legally barred from running. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate is widely expected to run for office in the event of an election, despite her exclusion from transition talks.
paras.zh: 反对派领袖玛丽亚·科里娜·马查多上个月出人意料地从流亡归来，震动了委内瑞拉政坛。马查多在 2023 年赢得反对派初选，并在次年的选举中与马杜罗较量，但法律禁止她参选。尽管这位诺贝尔和平奖获得者被排除在过渡谈判之外，但人们普遍预计她将在选举中竞选公职。

paras.en: Despite being shut out, on Thursday Machado launched a system of neighbourhood assemblies aiming to gather proposals for a future government programme and democratic transition. The assemblies are expected to bring together over a million people over several months, according to Machado’s team.
paras.zh: 尽管被拒之门外，马查多周四启动了一个社区集会制度，旨在收集有关未来政府计划和民主过渡的建议。据马查多的团队称，集会预计将在几个月内聚集超过一百万人。

paras.en: “We listened to neighbours who are breaking down barriers that many thought were impossible, debating the issues that will lay the foundations for the Venezuela to come,” Machado said on social media on Thursday after the meetings. “We are designing the transition to democracy, the Venezuelan way.”
paras.zh: 马查多周四在会后在社交媒体上表示：“我们听取了邻国的意见，他们正在打破许多人认为不可能的障碍，讨论将为委内瑞拉的未来奠定基础的问题。” “我们正在设计向民主的过渡，以委内瑞拉的方式。”

paras.en: Around 2,000 meetings with residents were organised in Venezuela and abroad on the first day of the initiative, her team told the AFP news agency.
paras.zh: 她的团队告诉法新社，该倡议第一天在委内瑞拉和国外组织了约 2,000 次与居民的会议。

paras.en: Nineteen questions are asked during the assembly, with responses fed into a digital platform. Issues of national interest range from dates for the presidential election to changes in the justice, education, health, wage and pension systems, as well as the role of the public and private sectors.
paras.zh: 大会期间提出了十九个问题，并将答案输入数字平台。国家利益问题的范围从总统选举的日期到司法、教育、卫生、工资和养老金制度的变化，以及公共和私营部门的作用。

articles.title: Why are families going hungry in northern Yemen even where food is on sale?

paras.en: Umm Sami, a widow raising four children in Yemen’s Red Sea port city of Hodeidah, sells household goods and takes on occasional domestic work to feed her family. Rising prices have changed how she shops. “Sometimes we buy a little flour or oil that lasts just one day because we cannot afford a whole bag,” she told Al Jazeera.
paras.zh: 乌姆·萨米 (Umm Sami) 是一名寡妇，在也门红海港口城市荷台达抚养着四个孩子，她靠出售家居用品并偶尔做家务来养家糊口。物价上涨改变了她的购物方式。 “有时我们买一点面粉或油，只够一天用，因为我们买不起一整袋，”她告诉半岛电视台。

paras.en: Food is still on the shelves. It was available in the markets that monitors could reach in September, but families had less money to spend, according to the Yemen Joint Monitoring Report, a humanitarian and food security assessment. Across Houthi-controlled areas like Hodeidah, a basket of basic foods cost about 7 percent, or $91, more that month than in August, its highest level in a year.
paras.zh: 食物仍在货架上。根据人道主义和粮食安全评估也门联合监测报告，监测人员 9 月份可以到达的市场上可以买到这种药物，但家庭可花的钱减少了。在荷台达等胡塞武装控制的地区，当月一篮子基本食品的价格约为 7%，即 91 美元，比 8 月份高出约 7%，为一年来的最高水平。

paras.en: Families on both sides of the front lines are struggling, and prices are rising faster in the government-held south, according to the Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET). What sets the Houthi-controlled north apart is how little families there can earn and how little help is left.
paras.zh: 根据饥荒预警系统网络 (FEWS NET) 的数据，前线两侧的家庭都在苦苦挣扎，政府控制的南部地区的物价上涨得更快。胡塞武装控制的北部地区的独特之处在于，那里的家庭能挣到的钱非常少，而且剩下的帮助也非常少。

paras.en: Most households in and around northern towns find only five to 10 days of paid work a month, FEWS NET reported in October. The UN World Food Programme’s (WFP) food assistance in Houthi-held areas has been suspended since September 2025, FEWS NET said. By mid-September 2026, WFP had begun a distribution round in government-held areas that aimed to reach about 1.7 million people.
paras.zh: 据 FEWS NET 10 月份报道，北部城镇及其周边地区的大多数家庭每月只能从事 5 至 10 天的带薪工作。 FEWS NET 称，联合国世界粮食计划署 ​​(WFP) 自 2025 年 9 月起暂停向胡塞武装控制地区提供粮食援助。到 2026 年 9 月中旬，粮食计划署已开始在政府控制的地区进行一轮分发，旨在惠及约 170 万人。

paras.en: In the last nationwide hunger analysis by UN agencies and their partners, published in mid-2025, the only people projected to face catastrophic hunger, about 41,000, were in four districts of Amran, Hodeidah and Hajjah governorates – all under Houthi control.
paras.zh: 在联合国机构及其合作伙伴于 2025 年年中发布的上一次全国饥饿分析中，预计将面临灾难性饥饿的人口约为 41,000 人，他们居住在阿姆兰省、荷台达省和哈杰省的四个地区，全部都在胡塞武装控制之下。

paras.en: On Friday, the WFP and the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) named Yemen among its hunger hotspots of highest concern for the six months ending May 2027.
paras.zh: 周五，粮食计划署和联合国粮食及农业组织 (FAO) 将也门列为截至 2027 年 5 月的六个月内最受关注的饥饿热点地区之一。

paras.en: As fighting spreads and aid dries up, we look at why food on sale in northern Yemen is slipping out of reach of the families who need it.
paras.zh: 随着战斗蔓延和援助枯竭，我们来看看为什么也门北部出售的食物越来越少，而有需要的家庭却买不到。

paras.en: Why are some families in Hodeidah buying food one day at a time?
paras.zh: 为什么荷台达的一些家庭一天一次地购买食物？

paras.en: Because a day’s work – when there is any – no longer pays for a day’s food.
paras.zh: 因为一天的工作——如果有的话——不再支付一天的食物。

paras.en: Ahmed Arjash drives a rented motorcycle taxi near Hodeidah’s Othman market to support his family of six. Many of his former customers now walk to save the fare. “Now, my daily earnings barely cover the fuel or the rent for the motorcycle,” he told Al Jazeera.
paras.zh: 艾哈迈德·阿尔贾什 (Ahmed Arjash) 在荷台达的奥斯曼市场附近驾驶着一辆租来的摩托车出租车来养活他的六口之家。他的许多以前的顾客现在步行以节省车费。 “现在，我每天的收入几乎不足以支付燃料或摩托车的租金，”他告诉半岛电视台。

paras.en: Saleh, a construction worker paid by the day, said some days pass without anyone hiring him. “If I work one day, the wage is not enough to cover the family’s needs for several days with prices this high,” he said.
paras.zh: 萨利赫是一名按日计酬的建筑工人，他说，有些日子过去了，没有人雇用他。 “如果我有一天工作，在物价这么高的情况下，工资还不够一家人几天的需要，”他说。

paras.en: Fishing pays less, too. Salem, a fisherman in his 30s, said fuel, boats and equipment cost him more while fewer customers could afford his catch. “Many families no longer buy fish as they used to,” he said. On some trips, he barely earns back what it costs to go to sea.
paras.zh: 钓鱼的钱也更少。 30 多岁的渔民塞勒姆表示，燃料、船只和设备的成本更高，而能够负担得起他捕获的鱼的顾客却更少。 “许多家庭不再像以前那样买鱼，”他说。在某些旅行中，他勉强赚回出海的费用。

paras.en: Families are adjusting by eating less. In Hodeidah’s poorest neighbourhoods, many skip meals or go without meat, fish, milk and fruit, Al Jazeera found.
paras.zh: 家人正在通过少吃来进行调整。半岛电视台发现，在荷台达最贫困的社区，许多人不吃饭或不吃肉、鱼、牛奶和水果。

paras.en: In Houthi-held areas, FEWS NET reported that higher taxes on street vendors and shops had already reduced demand for labour in September. In its outlook through May 2027, it expected more small businesses to close and those that stayed open to hire fewer workers.
paras.zh: FEWS NET 报道称，在胡塞武装控制的地区，对街头小贩和商店征收的更高税收已经减少了 9 月份的劳动力需求。在截至 2027 年 5 月的展望中，预计将有更多小型企业关闭，而那些继续营业的企业将雇用更少的工人。

paras.en: How does food reach shops in northern Yemen, and what makes the journey more expensive?
paras.zh: 食物如何到达也门北部的商店？是什么导致旅程更加昂贵？

paras.en: Almost all of it comes by sea, and each step from ship to shop now costs more. Yemen imports about 90 percent of its food, according to WFP. Hodeidah is the main port supplying the Houthi-held north, including Sanaa.
paras.zh: 几乎所有货物都是通过海运运输的，现在从船到商店的每一步成本都更高。据世界粮食计划署称，也门约 90% 的粮食依赖进口。荷台达是向胡塞武装控制的北部地区（包括萨那）供应物资的主要港口。

paras.en: Food has kept arriving – data shows imports into Houthi-held areas rose 10 percent between June and August compared with the previous three months and doubled year-on-year – but fuel has not.
paras.zh: 食品源源不断地运抵——数据显示，6 月至 8 月期间，胡塞武装控制地区的进口量比前三个月增加了 10%，同比翻了一番——但燃料却没有。

paras.en: Fuel imports fell about 85 percent year-on-year in August, with no recorded arrivals of diesel or petrol through northern ports, according to the FAO. In September, the Houthi authorities raised the price of petrol by about 10 percent, the first increase in four years, Al Jazeera reported. Bread prices in Houthi-held areas rose 25 percent that month, FEWS NET said.
paras.zh: 据粮农组织称，8 月份燃料进口量同比下降约 85%，没有记录到北部港口有柴油或汽油抵达。据半岛电视台报道，9 月，胡塞武装当局将汽油价格提高了约 10%，这是四年来的首次上调。 FEWS NET 称，当月胡塞武装控制地区的面包价格上涨了 25%。

paras.en: The ports themselves have come under attack. On November 2, the Houthi-run Al Masirah TV said Saudi aircraft had hit a pier and a commercial ship at Ras Isa port, north of Hodeidah, the news agency AFP reported. On Tuesday, the Saudi-led coalition said it had attacked “operational capabilities” in Hodeidah, and the Houthis threatened to retaliate against Saudi Red Sea ports. Hodeidah port remains open, Al Jazeera reported. How the latest attacks will affect deliveries remains unclear.
paras.zh: 港口本身也受到了攻击。据法新社报道，11 月 2 日，胡塞武装控制的 Al Masirah 电视台称，沙特飞机撞上了荷台达北部拉斯伊萨港的一个码头和一艘商船。周二，沙特领导的联军表示袭击了荷台达的“作战能力”，胡塞武装威胁要对沙特红海港口进行报复。据半岛电视台报道，荷台达港口仍然开放。目前尚不清楚最新的攻击将如何影响交付。

paras.en: Moving goods inland has also become slower and costlier. A truck travelling between the south and the north “now takes up to a week to reach its final destination”, Saleh Abdullah, a shopkeeper in Sanaa, told Al Jazeera in September. Before the renewed fighting, the trip took three days or less. Customers pay the extra transport and fuel costs, he said. “Whether it is the flour, the baby milk, the fruits, the vegetables, or anything else.”
paras.zh: 向内陆运输货物也变得更慢、成本更高。萨那的店主萨利赫·阿卜杜拉 (Saleh Abdullah) 9 月份告诉半岛电视台，一辆往返于南部和北部之间的卡车“现在需要长达一周的时间才能到达最终目的地”。在战斗重新开始之前，这次旅行只花了三天或更短的时间。他说，客户支付额外的运输和燃料费用。 “无论是面粉、婴儿奶粉、水果、蔬菜还是其他任何东西。”

paras.en: When families cannot afford food, what stops aid from reaching them?
paras.zh: 当家庭买不起食物时，是什么阻止他们获得援助？

paras.en: In the north, the main source of food aid has been switched off. WFP suspended its activities in Houthi-controlled areas in September 2025 after the group detained UN staff. Last month, WFP said 73 UN personnel, 38 of them its own staff, remained in detention.
paras.zh: 在北部，粮食援助的主要来源已被切断。 2025 年 9 月，胡塞武装拘留联合国工作人员后，粮食计划署暂停了在胡塞武装控制地区的活动。粮食计划署上个月表示，73 名联合国人员仍被拘留，其中 38 名是其自己的工作人员。

paras.en: Other aid organisations still operate in the north, but funding cuts and restrictions limit their reach.
paras.zh: 其他援助组织仍在北部开展活动，但资金削减和限制限制了其范围。

paras.en: On Thursday, the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) said a handful of overstretched and underfunded Yemeni and international organisations were the only remaining lifeline for millions there.
paras.zh: 周四，挪威难民理事会（NRC）表示，一些捉襟见肘且资金不足的也门和国际组织是那里数百万人的唯一生命线。

paras.en: Funding cuts, sanctions and the UN’s pause in operations had all contributed to a collapsing humanitarian response, it added. The NRC said donors had provided just 16 percent of the money sought for food security across Yemen this year.
paras.zh: 报告补充说，资金削减、制裁和联合国行动暂停都导致了人道主义救援行动的崩溃。 NRC 表示，捐助者仅提供了今年也门粮食安全所需资金的 16%。

paras.en: What does the UN’s new hunger warning tell us about northern Yemen?
paras.zh: 关于也门北部，联合国新的饥饿警告告诉我们什么？

paras.en: The latest FAO–WFP report warns that fighting and economic hardship threaten to deepen hunger through May 2027. It names economic hardship among the threats, but it cannot say how many people in the north are going hungry. FAO and WFP said conflict, displacement, economic hardship and extreme weather drove the risk in the five hotspots of highest concern, the Reuters news agency reported.
paras.zh: 粮农组织-粮食计划署最新报告警告称，到 2027 年 5 月，战斗和经济困难可能会加剧饥饿。报告将经济困难列为威胁之一，但无法说明北方有多少人正在挨饿。据路透社报道，粮农组织和粮食计划署表示，冲突、流离失所、经济困难和极端天气加剧了五个最受关注的热点地区的风险。

paras.en: The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), the UN-backed system for measuring hunger, has not published a recent analysis of Houthi-held areas. Its latest figures – 5.4 million people facing crisis levels of hunger or worse between October and December, including 1.8 million at the more severe emergency level – cover government-held areas only.
paras.zh: 联合国支持的饥饿衡量系统综合粮食安全阶段分类（IPC）尚未发布对胡塞武装控制地区的最新分析。其最新数据——10月至12月期间有540万人面临饥饿危机或更严重的程度，其中180万人处于更严重的紧急状态——仅涵盖政府控制的地区。

paras.en: In June 2025, the IPC projected that 18.1 million people in Yemen would face crisis levels of hunger or worse between September 2025 and February 2026. That was 52 percent of the population covered by the nationwide analysis.
paras.zh: 2025 年 6 月，IPC 预测，2025 年 9 月至 2026 年 2 月期间，也门将有 1810 万人面临饥饿危机或更严重的情况。这占全国分析覆盖人口的 52%。

paras.en: FEWS NET expects emergency levels of hunger to persist in Hodeidah and Hajjah through May 2027.
paras.zh: FEWS NET 预计荷台达和哈贾的紧急饥饿水平将持续到 2027 年 5 月。

paras.en: At that level, families face large gaps in what they eat, or must sell what they need to make a living to buy food. The network’s gravest warning concerns Taiz, a government-held city besieged by Houthi forces, where it sees a credible risk of famine between February and May if the siege is prolonged and tightened.
paras.zh: 在这个水平上，家庭在吃的方面面临着巨大的差距，或者必须出售他们谋生所需的东西来购买食物。该网络最严重的警告涉及塔伊兹，这是一个被胡塞武装围困的政府控制城市，该网络认为，如果围困时间延长并收紧，该地区在 2 月至 5 月期间将面临发生饥荒的风险。

paras.en: In Hodeidah, the market still has flour. For families like Umm Sami’s, the question is how little of it they can afford. “Even bread has become a burden,” she said.
paras.zh: 在荷台达，市场上还有面粉。对于像乌姆萨米这样的家庭来说，问题是他们能负担得起的费用有多少。 “连面包都成了负担，”她说。

articles.title: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
articles.author: Ari Daniel

paras.en: How American Thanksgiving took root — and evolved — in Liberia
paras.zh: 美国感恩节如何在利比里亚扎根并演变

paras.en: Yvonne Capehart Weah is from Liberia, a country in West Africa, and she's one of twelve siblings.
paras.zh: 伊冯·卡普哈特·维阿 (Yvonne Capehart Weah) 来自西非国家利比里亚，是十二个兄弟姐妹之一。

paras.en: "I'm the second to the last one — I'm the eleventh," she says. "We have large families in Liberia."
paras.zh: “我是倒数第二个——我是第十一个，”她说。 “我们在利比里亚有很多家庭。”

paras.en: Every year on the first Thursday in November, Weah's family gathers in Caldwell, the township where she grew up, to celebrate Liberian Thanksgiving.
paras.zh: 每年十一月的第一个星期四，维阿的家人都会聚集在她长大的小镇考德威尔，庆祝利比里亚感恩节。

paras.en: "When we come together, the group become [so] large that you are not able to sit around a dining table," she explains. "So we do it outside under the tree. And when we meet, it's almost like we're having a party."
paras.zh: “当我们聚在一起时，这个群体变得如此之大，以至于你无法坐在餐桌旁，”她解释道。 “所以我们在外面的树下进行。当我们见面时，几乎就像我们正在举办派对一样。”

paras.en: The Liberian holiday dates back to the first half of the 19th century when the American Colonization Society established the community that would grow into the country. It was founded by Black Americans — both those born free and enslaved people who had been emancipated — whose departure was sometimes voluntary, sometimes forced. "The settlers from America brought that Thanksgiving Day tradition to Liberia," says Weah. Once transplanted, the holiday evolved over time in response to national events.
paras.zh: 利比里亚的节日可以追溯到 19 世纪上半叶，当时美国殖民协会建立了后来发展到该国的社区。它是由美国黑人创立的——包括那些生来自由的人和获得解放的奴隶——他们的离开有时是自愿的，有时是被迫的。 “来自美国的定居者将感恩节传统带到了利比里亚，”维阿说。一旦移植，这个节日就会随着时间的推移而演变，以响应全国性的事件。

paras.en: Liberia gained its independence in 1847 but the British continued trying to take swaths of territory. In 1883, President Alfred Francis Russell, an Episcopalian priest, called upon God to help halt the incursions.
paras.zh: 利比里亚于 1847 年获得独立，但英国人继续试图占领大片领土。 1883 年，圣公会牧师阿尔弗雷德·弗朗西斯·拉塞尔总统呼吁上帝帮助阻止入侵。

paras.en: That invocation was a "prayer of protection against the intruders, preventing intrusion into our territory," says Weah.
paras.zh: 维阿说，这一祈祷是“祈祷免受入侵者的侵害，防止入侵我们的领土”。

paras.en: The Liberians managed to maintain their sovereignty. And that year, the legislature officially established Thanksgiving as a national holiday steeped in the religious gratitude of the moment.
paras.zh: 利比里亚人设法维护了自己的主权。那一年，立法机关正式将感恩节定为全国性节日，充满了宗教感恩之情。

paras.en: Weah summarizes Liberian Thanksgiving this way: "It's giving thanks to God for our freedom, for divine protection. It's giving thanks to God for unity and for the harvest."
paras.zh: 维阿这样总结利比里亚的感恩节：“感谢上帝赐予我们的自由，感谢上帝的保护。感谢上帝赐予我们团结和丰收。”

paras.en: Weah says that her family's celebration, like that of many others in Liberia, starts in the morning at church. But the holiday's for people of all faiths, and other religious communities mark the occasion as well
paras.zh: 维阿说，她家人的庆祝活动和利比里亚其他许多人的庆祝活动一样，从早上在教堂开始。但这个节日适合所有信仰的人，其他宗教团体也庆祝这个节日

paras.en: "The Muslims, they go to the mosques and pray," says Sekou Muhammad Sheriff, a YouTuber who travels his home country of Liberia to showcase its offerings and cultural heritage, including Thanksgiving. "And Muslims, Christians, and others — everybody observe this day as a holiday."
paras.zh: “穆斯林会去清真寺祈祷，”YouTuber Sekou Muhammad Sheriff 说道，他前往自己的祖国利比里亚展示其产品和文化遗产，包括感恩节。 “穆斯林、基督徒和其他人——每个人都把这一天当作节日。”

paras.en: When Sheriff was a boy, this was the day that he counted on to get a new outfit.
paras.zh: 当警长还是个孩子的时候，他就指望着这一天能得到一套新衣服。

paras.en: "What my dad used to do for me," says Sheriff, was to purchase a "shirt-trouser suit, and then he'd buy me slipper." His favorite suit was a white one.
paras.zh: 警长说：“我父亲过去常常为我买一套“衬衫裤套装，然后他会给我买一双拖鞋。”他最喜欢的西装是白色的。

paras.en: Over the years on Thanksgiving, he's grown accustomed to eating different stews, including one made with sweet potato leaves and another with snails collected from the garden.
paras.zh: 多年来，他已经习惯在感恩节吃不同的炖菜，其中一种是用红薯叶做的，另一种是用从花园里收集的蜗牛做的。

paras.en: "We call it king's meat," Sheriff says with a chuckle. "It is very, very nice."
paras.zh: “我们称之为国王的肉，”警长笑着说道。 “这非常非常好。”

paras.en: The mid-afternoon meal varies from household to household in Liberia.
paras.zh: 在利比里亚，每个家庭的午饭时间各不相同。

paras.en: "We don't do turkey," says Weah, "but we do chicken. We do fried chicken, smoked chicken, roasted chicken."
paras.zh: “我们不做火鸡，”维阿说，“但我们做鸡肉。我们做炸鸡、熏鸡、烤鸡。”

paras.en: Weah's family also serves jollof rice, watermelon, pineapple and a variety of stews, including one called fufu and soup. It's a mix of cassava, fish, chicken, okra, chili pepper and more. "That makes the soup very tasty," says Weah. "It has to be [at] every Thanksgiving."
paras.zh: 维阿的家人还提供乔洛夫米饭、西瓜、菠萝和各种炖菜，包括一种叫做“fufu”和“汤”的炖菜。它是木薯、鱼、鸡肉、秋葵、辣椒等的混合物。 “这使得汤非常美味，”维阿说。 “它必须是在每个感恩节。”

paras.en: (Weah doesn't especially like to cook, however. "If you tell me, 'Go in the kitchen to cook or sit in the living room and read,'" she says, "I will sit in the living room and read.")
paras.zh: （然而，维阿并不是特别喜欢做饭。“如果你告诉我，‘去厨房做饭，或者坐在客厅里读书，’”她说，“我会坐在客厅里读书。”）

paras.en: This year, Sheriff didn't have the resources to host Thanksgiving. But he says that he remains thankful to God for keeping him healthy and for keeping Liberia peaceful after civil conflict tore his country apart from 1989 to 1997 and 1999 to 2003.
paras.zh: 今年，警长没有资源举办感恩节。但他说，他仍然感谢上帝让他保持健康，并在 1989 年至 1997 年和 1999 年至 2003 年的内战使利比里亚分裂后保持利比里亚的和平。

paras.en: Weah is also grateful. "When I go for Thanksgiving," she says, "I'm thanking God for where I have come from, where I am now, and I'm also thanking Him for where He will take me because I know He holds the future."
paras.zh: 维阿也很感激。 “当我去过感恩节时，”她说，“我感谢上帝让我从哪里来，现在在哪里，我也感谢他将带我去哪里，因为我知道他掌握着未来。”

paras.en: Weah is the program manager at the We-Care Foundation, an education nonprofit that, among other things, teaches children literacy. "A reading child will become a reading elder," she says.
paras.zh: 维阿是 We-Care 基金会的项目经理，该基金会是一家教育非营利组织，其业务之一是教授儿童识字。 “一个读书的孩子将会成为一个读书的老人，”她说。

paras.en: "And we expect informed adults to make informed decisions that affect both their social and economic life" — in ways, perhaps, that they will one day be thankful for.
paras.zh: “我们希望知情的成年人能够做出明智的决定，影响他们的社会和经济生活”——也许，他们有一天会对此心存感激。

articles.title: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
articles.author: Michele Kelemen

paras.en: As UN Secretary General's last day approaches, search for his replacement continues
paras.zh: 随着联合国秘书长最后一天的临近，寻找继任者的工作仍在继续

paras.en: The UN Secretary General's term ends this year, but the big powers at the UN have been unable to agree on a replacement. UN watchers worry that there will be little time to get up to speed.
paras.zh: 联合国秘书长的任期将于今年结束，但联合国各大国一直未能就继任者达成一致。联合国观察人士担心，几乎没有时间加快步伐。

paras.en: It's crunch time for the U.N., as it looks to appoint its next secretary-general. Antonio Guterres is due to step down next month. But after nine rounds of straw polls in the Security Council, there's still no consensus on a successor. Here's NPR's Michele Kelemen.
paras.zh: 对于联合国来说，现在是任命下一任秘书长的关键时刻。安东尼奥·古特雷斯将于下个月辞职。但安理会经过九轮投票后，仍未就继任者达成共识。请听 NPR 的米歇尔·克莱门 (Michele Kelemen) 的报道。

paras.en: MICHELE KELEMEN, BYLINE: The Trump administration has been tight-lipped about its preferences for a new secretary-general and had been holding out hope for new candidates to jump in the race. But time is running out, says former U.S. Ambassador Robert Wood.
paras.zh: 米歇尔·克莱门连线：特朗普政府一直对新秘书长的偏好守口如瓶，并一直对新候选人加入竞选抱有希望。但前美国大使罗伯特·伍德表示，时间已经不多了。

paras.en: ROBERT WOOD: I think it's too late, and I'm not sure anybody would want to enter the race at this particular point.
paras.zh: 罗伯特·伍德：我认为为时已晚，而且我不确定是否有人愿意在这个特定时刻参加比赛。

paras.en: KELEMEN: He says there's too much at stake.
paras.zh: 克莱门：他说风险太大了。

paras.en: WOOD: Given the turmoil that we have in the world, all these raging wars, the bad need for the U.N. to be reformed, confidence in the U.N. at an all-time low, we need to get this decision right. It has to be the right person.
paras.zh: 伍德：鉴于世界上的动荡、所有这些激烈的战争、联合国改革的迫切需要以及对联合国的信心处于历史最低点，我们需要做出正确的决定。一定是对的人。

paras.en: KELEMEN: Wood sees this mostly as a race between two candidates - Rebeca Grynspan, a former vice president of Costa Rica who's led the U.N.'s Trade and Development Organization, and Italian Argentinian Rafael Grossi, who heads the U.N.'s nuclear watchdog. Guyana's former foreign minister and U.N. ambassador, Carolyn Rodrigues-Burkett, is also in the mix. A former ambassador from the United Arab Emirates, Lana Nusseibeh, is, too, though she's facing opposition from activists because of her country's support for a militia carrying out atrocities in Sudan. Latin American countries also say that this is their region's turn to lead the U.N., according to U.N. traditions of regional rotations.
paras.zh: 克莱门：伍德认为这主要是两位候选人之间的竞争——领导联合国贸易和发展组织的哥斯达黎加前副总统丽贝卡·格林斯潘和领导联合国核监督机构的意大利人阿根廷人拉斐尔·格罗西。圭亚那前外交部长兼联合国大使卡罗琳·罗德里格斯·伯克特也在其中。阿拉伯联合酋长国前大使拉娜·努赛贝 (Lana Nusseibeh) 也是如此，不过她面临活动人士的反对，因为她的国家支持民兵在苏丹实施暴行。拉美国家也表示，根据联合国区域轮流的传统，现在轮到他们所在地区领导联合国了。

paras.en: ELIZABETH COUSENS: It's a confounding process at this point because it is a very strong field.
paras.zh: ELIZABETH COUSENS：这是一个令人困惑的过程，因为这是一个非常强大的领域。

paras.en: KELEMEN: That's Elizabeth Cousens, president of the U.N. Foundation, which advocates for a strong U.S. presence at the U.N. In the straw polls, all four of these top candidates have faced opposition from two or more permanent Security Council members. Cousens says it's time for the council to rally behind someone to get the candidate to the General Assembly floor before the year is up.
paras.zh: 克莱门：这位是伊丽莎白·库森斯，联合国基金会主席，该基金会主张美国在联合国拥有强大的存在。在这次民意调查中，这四位最重要的候选人都遭到了两个或两个以上安理会常任理事国的反对。库森斯表示，现在是理事会团结起来支持某人的时候了，以便在年底前让候选人进入大会发言。

paras.en: COUSENS: It's a group of really capable people who've led institutions. They've reformed institutions. They've led negotiations. They've been in the front line of major geopolitical files. I mean, this is a serious group of people running for this role, and I do think it's important to give the field credit for that.
paras.zh: COUSENS：这是一群真正有能力的人领导着机构。他们改革了机构。他们主导了谈判。他们一直处于主要地缘政治文件的最前线。我的意思是，这是一群认真的人在竞选这个角色，我确实认为给予该领域的荣誉很重要。

paras.en: KELEMEN: Another U.N. watcher, Anjali Dayal, who teaches international politics at Fordham University, says whoever emerges will have little time to get up to speed at a complicated time in world affairs.
paras.zh: 克莱门：另一位联合国观察员、在福特汉姆大学教授国际政治的安贾利·达亚尔表示，在世界事务的复杂时期，无论谁出现，都没有时间跟上进度。

paras.en: ANJALI DAYAL: We would never think that a private organization appointing someone in December to pick up the reins in January would be a good idea. We would not imagine that we would give them that little lead time to take over the stewardship of a massive, complicated organization - to staff up, to be briefed, to hit the ground running.
paras.zh: ANJALI DAYAL：我们绝不会认为一个私人组织在 12 月任命某人在一月份接手权力会是一个好主意。我们不会想象我们会给他们那么短的准备时间来接管一个庞大而复杂的组织的管理工作——安排人员、听取简报、开始运作。

paras.en: KELEMEN: The State Department says it wants a secretary-general to get back to basics, working on peace and security rather than, quote, "the absurd, politicized, woke ideology that has undermined" the U.N.'s effectiveness. Dayal points out that the Trump administration did not go through the U.N. to launch a war against Iran, and Russia violated the U.N. Charter by invading Ukraine.
paras.zh: 克莱门：美国国务院表示，希望秘书长回归本源，致力于和平与安全，而不是引用“削弱联合国有效性的荒谬、政治化、觉醒的意识形态”。达亚尔指出，特朗普政府没有通过联合国对伊朗发动战争，俄罗斯入侵乌克兰也违反了《联合国宪章》。

paras.en: DAYAL: And so being able to get this position involves satisfying permanent members that want to violate the terms of the Charter while committing to upholding the terms of the Charter - to hold the job, to perform it well for everybody else. So it's a tricky proposition, and that's why it's taking so long.
paras.zh: 戴亚尔：因此，要想获得这个职位，就需要满足那些想要违反《宪章》条款的常任理事国的要求，同时承诺维护《宪章》的条款——保住这份工作，为其他人做好工作。所以这是一个棘手的提议，这就是为什么它花了这么长时间。

paras.en: KELEMEN: Behind the scenes, U.N. experts say there's probably some horse trading going on that could include promises of top U.N. jobs to permanent Security Council members to overcome veto threats.
paras.zh: 克莱门：联合国专家表示，在幕后，可能存在一些讨价还价的行为，其中可能包括向安理会常任理事国承诺提供联合国最高职位，以克服否决权威胁。

paras.en: Michele Kelemen, NPR News, the State Department.
paras.zh: 米歇尔·凯莱门 (Michele Kelemen)，美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 新闻，国务院。

articles.title: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
articles.author: The Associated Press

paras.en: French cinema star Gérard Depardieu ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault
paras.zh: 法国电影明星杰拉尔·德帕迪约因强奸和性侵犯被判受审

paras.en: PARIS — Gérard Depardieu, for decades one of France's most celebrated actors, has been ordered to stand trial on charges of raping and sexually assaulting a young actress, authorities said Thursday, less than two weeks after the cinema star abandoned his appeal of a sexual assault conviction in a separate case.
paras.zh: 巴黎——当局周四称，几十年来法国最著名的演员之一热拉尔·德帕迪约因强奸和性侵犯一名年轻女演员的指控而被下令接受审判，距离这位电影明星放弃对另一起案件中性侵犯定罪的上诉不到两周。

paras.en: Actress Charlotte Arnould was 22 when she accused Depardieu in 2018 of raping her at his Paris home.
paras.zh: 2018 年，女演员夏洛特·阿诺德 (Charlotte Arnould) 指控德帕迪约 (Depardieu) 在他位于巴黎的家中强奸她，当时她只有 22 岁。

paras.en: Eight years later, the Paris Court of Appeal ruled that the actor should face trial over allegations of rape and sexual assault on Aug. 7, 2018, while dismissing allegations relating to a second incident six days later.
paras.zh: 八年后，巴黎上诉法院于 2018 年 8 月 7 日裁定，这位演员应因强奸和性侵犯指控接受审判，同时驳回了六天后与第二起事件有关的指控。

paras.en: Depardieu, 77, has denied the rape allegations. His lawyer, Delphine Meillet, told The Associated Press that he disputes Thursday's ruling, without specifying whether he would challenge it before France's highest court for civil and criminal cases.
paras.zh: 77 岁的德帕迪约否认了强奸指控。他的律师德尔菲娜·梅耶 (Delphine Meil​​let) 告诉美联社，他对周四的裁决提出异议，但没有具体说明他是否会向法国最高法院民事和刑事案件提出质疑。

paras.en: The ruling upholds part of an investigating judge's August 2025 decision to send Depardieu to trial.
paras.zh: 该裁决维持了调查法官 2025 年 8 月将德帕迪约送审的决定的部分内容。

paras.en: The case has become one of the most prominent in France's reckoning with sexual violence, as the #MeToo movement has faced resistance in the country, particularly in the arts.
paras.zh: 由于“#MeToo”运动在法国面临阻力，尤其是在艺术领域，该案件已成为法国处理性暴力问题中最突出的案件之一。

paras.en: A French cinema icon faces a #MeToo reckoning
paras.zh: 法国电影偶像面临#MeToo清算

paras.en: With his hulking frame, crooked nose and commanding screen presence, Depardieu dominated French cinema for half a century.
paras.zh: 德帕迪约凭借其魁梧的身材、鹰钩鼻和霸气的银幕形象，统治了法国电影半个世纪。

paras.en: He became one of the country's most recognizable cultural exports, earning an Oscar nomination for "Cyrano de Bergerac" and a Golden Globe for "Green Card."
paras.zh: 他成为该国最知名的文化输出者之一，凭借《西拉诺·德·贝尔热拉克》获得奥斯卡提名，并凭借《绿卡》获得金球奖。

paras.en: But accusations of sexual misconduct and his subsequent conviction have increasingly overshadowed his cinematic legacy.
paras.zh: 但对性行为不端的指控以及随后的定罪日益掩盖了他的电影遗产。

paras.en: On Nov. 16, Depardieu abandoned his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set in 2021, accepting an 18-month suspended prison sentence and issuing a public apology that marked a departure from his earlier denials in that case.
paras.zh: 11 月 16 日，德帕迪约放弃了对因在 2021 年拍摄的电影中性侵两名女性而被定罪的上诉，接受 18 个月的缓刑，并公开道歉，这标志着他与之前对该案的否认有所不同。

paras.en: "I therefore offer my deep and sincere apologies to those who may have suffered," he said in a written statement.
paras.zh: 他在一份书面声明中说：“因此，我向那些可能遭受苦难的人致以深切而真诚的歉意。”

paras.en: Depardieu was convicted in May 2025 of groping a set decorator and an assistant during the filming of "Les Volets Verts" ("The Green Shutters").
paras.zh: 2025 年 5 月，德帕迪约因在拍摄《绿色百叶窗》期间猥亵一名布景师和一名助理而被定罪。

paras.en: The court also ordered his name to be listed in France's national sex offender database.
paras.zh: 法院还下令将他的名字列入法国国家性犯罪者数据库。

paras.en: "On film sets, I have long hidden behind provocation and crude humor. I believed my words and some of my actions had no consequences. But they did, particularly coming from someone who held as much power as I once did," Depardieu said.
paras.zh: “在电影片场，我长期以来一直隐藏在挑衅和粗俗的幽默背后。我相信我的话语和我的一些行为不会产生任何后果。但它们确实会产生后果，特别是来自像我曾经一样拥有权力的人，”德帕迪约说。

paras.en: Accusations against Depardieu sparked a national debate
paras.zh: 对德帕迪约的指控引发全国辩论

paras.en: The controversy surrounding Depardieu intensified in December 2023 after a television documentary showed him repeatedly making obscene remarks and gestures during a 2018 trip to North Korea.
paras.zh: 2023 年 12 月，一部电视纪录片显示德帕迪约在 2018 年朝鲜之行期间多次发表猥亵言论和手势，围绕德帕迪约的争议愈演愈烈。

paras.en: Even French President Emmanuel Macron weighed in, drawing criticism from women's rights activists when he said the actor "makes France proud." Macron invoked the presumption of innocence and said he would not participate in a "manhunt."
paras.zh: 就连法国总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙(Emmanuel Macron)也发表了自己的看法，称这位演员“让法国感到自豪”，此举招致了女权活动人士的批评。马克龙援引无罪推定原则，表示他不会参与“搜捕”。

paras.en: The controversy exposed divisions in a country where some prominent cultural figures had pushed back against the #MeToo movement.
paras.zh: 这场争议暴露了这个国家的分歧，一些著名文化人物反对#MeToo运动。

paras.en: In 2018, actress Catherine Deneuve and 99 other women signed an open letter defending men's freedom to make advances toward women and warning against what they saw as the movement's excesses.
paras.zh: 2018 年，女演员凯瑟琳·德纳芙和其他 99 名女性签署了一封公开信，捍卫男性向女性示好的自由，并对她们认为的该运动的过度行为提出警告。

paras.en: Born in 1948 into a working-class family in the central French city of Châteauroux, Depardieu overcame a speech impediment to become one of France's most prolific actors. His career spanned hundreds of films, from "The Last Metro" and "Jean de Florette" to the popular "Asterix" franchise.
paras.zh: 德帕迪约 1948 年出生于法国中部城市沙托鲁的一个工人阶级家庭，他克服了语言障碍，成为法国最多产的演员之一。他的职业生涯跨越了数百部电影，从《最后的地铁》和《Jean de Florette》到广受欢迎的《Asterix》系列。

paras.en: His excesses off-screen also made international headlines, notably when he accepted a Russian passport from Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2013 amid a dispute over French taxes.
paras.zh: 他在银幕外的过激行为也成为国际头条新闻，特别是在 2013 年因法国税收争议而接受俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京 (Vladimir Putin) 颁发的俄罗斯护照时。
