paras.en: The teenager ultimately chose Harvard University. He fell in love with math once he got there. “He distinguished himself even in that class of overachieving first-years,” says Noam Elkies of Harvard, who was his math professor that year, “finding more than half the corrections in class materials that I did not notice sooner.” Other instructors noted Alpöge’s fastidiousness could cause tensions: in a recent Bluesky post, physicist Matt Reece recalled how the young Alpöge joined Reece’s graduate physics course and so angered the students with his persistent mathematical questions that “I feared someone would actually punch him in class.”
paras.zh: 这位少年最终选择了哈佛大学。他一到那里就爱上了数学。 “即使在一年级成绩优异的班级中，他也表现出色，”当年担任他的数学教授、哈佛大学的诺姆·埃尔基斯 (Noam Elkies) 说，“他在课堂材料中找到了一半以上我没有注意到的更正。”其他老师指出阿尔波格的挑剔可能会引起紧张：在最近的一篇 Bluesky 帖子中，物理学家马特·里斯回忆起年轻的阿尔波格如何加入里斯的研究生物理课程，并因他顽固的数学问题激怒了学生，以至于“我担心有人会在课堂上打他。”

paras.en: By his junior year, Alpöge was under the tutelage of renowned mathematician Jacob Tsimerman. (A few months ago Tsimerman won a Fields Medal, math’s highest honor, and then announced he was leaving academia to work on AI safety.)
paras.zh: 到大三时，阿尔波格就师从著名数学家雅各布·齐默曼 (Jacob Tsimerman)。 （几个月前，齐默曼获得了菲尔兹奖，这是数学的最高荣誉，然后宣布他将离开学术界，从事人工智能安全方面的工作。）

paras.en: That year Alpöge participated in a well-known summer undergraduate research program at the University of Minnesota Duluth. The program’s longtime leader, Joe Gallian, recalls Alpöge as unusually buoyant and charismatic. After visiting the program, mathematician Rishi Nath said to Gallian, “Everybody wants to be like Levent.”
paras.zh: 那一年，Alpöge 参加了明尼苏达大学德卢斯分校著名的暑期本科生研究项目。该项目的长期领导者 Joe Gallian 回忆道，Alpöge 异常活跃且富有魅力。数学家 Rishi Nath 在参观完该项目后对 Gallian 说：“每个人都想成为 Levent 那样的人。”

paras.en: Alpöge did groundbreaking work that summer, publishing papers in top journals that were on par with those of established professionals. With two weeks left, Gallian gave Alpöge a particularly hard problem to occupy his remaining time. Gallan said, “Work on it until classes start, and then, if you don’t have anything, it’s fine.” But Alpöge told him, “I’ll work on it until I solve it.”
paras.zh: 那年夏天，阿尔波格做了开创性的工作，在顶级期刊上发表了与知名专业人士的论文相当的论文。还剩两周时间，加利安给阿尔波格出了一道特别难的题，以打发他剩余的时间。加兰说：“一直努力到开课，然后，如果你没有任何东西，也没关系。”但阿尔波格告诉他：“我会继续努力，直到解决为止。”

paras.en: He showed similar tenacity for everything in life, Gallian says. During the Duluth group’s yearly stop at a restaurant called Betty’s Pies along Minnesota State Highway 61, three students volunteered for the “pig’s trough” challenge: if they could eat a massive pie stuffed with ice cream in 15 minutes, they’d win a free T-shirt. Alpöge did it in three minutes and 43 seconds—a record at the time.* He also ran Duluth’s annual marathon, and Gallian snapped a photograph of him outracing everybody at an “alpine sliding” course. “You can see the competitiveness and the fierceness and the power of concentration,” Gallian says.
paras.zh: 加利安说，他对生活中的一切都表现出了类似的坚韧。德卢斯小组每年都会在明尼苏达州 61 号公路沿线的一家名为 Betty’s Pies 的餐厅停留期间，三名学生自愿参加“猪槽”挑战：如果他们能在 15 分钟内吃掉一个巨大的冰淇淋馅饼，他们将赢得一件免费 T 恤。阿尔波格用时 3 分 43 秒完成了这一任务，创下了当时的纪录。*他还参加了德卢斯的年度马拉松比赛，加利安拍了一张他在“高山滑行”路线上超越所有人的照片。 “你可以看到竞争力、激烈程度和专注的力量，”加利安说。

paras.en: The following year Alpöge’s undergraduate thesis, about famous equations called “elliptic curves,” won him the illustrious Morgan Prize. In a recommendation letter, the late Harvard professor Benedict Gross called it “a tremendous piece of research for an undergraduate, at the level of an outstanding PhD thesis.” Perhaps, Gross speculated in his letter, something like a Fields Medal was in Alpöge’s future, too. Tsimerman struck a similar note in a recommendation of his own: “Often it seemed as if there was no way to proceed, and I even suggested switching problems a few times when I thought there was a dead end,” he wrote. “But Levent enjoyed the challenge too much to stop.”
paras.zh: 第二年，阿尔波格的本科论文涉及著名的“椭圆曲线”方程，为他赢得了著名的摩根奖。已故哈佛大学教授本尼迪克特·格罗斯（Benedict Gross）在一封推荐信中称其为“对于本科生来说是一项伟大的研究，达到了杰出博士论文的水平”。格罗斯在信中推测，也许阿尔波格的未来也会获得菲尔兹奖之类的东西。齐默尔曼在自己的建议中也表达了类似的观点：“通常情况下，似乎没有办法继续下去，当我认为有一个死胡同时，我什至建议几次转换问题，”他写道。 “但莱文特太享受这个挑战了，无法停止。”

paras.en: Alpöge added to his illustrious CV with a Ph.D. from Princeton University and postdoctoral position back at Harvard. His doctoral advisor, the Fields Medalist Manjul Bhargava, cites the same exuberance and talent but adds that Alpöge “was slow to write up the new things he did, in part because he was always thinking about so many things.”
paras.zh: Alpöge 在他杰出的简历中增添了博士学位。从普林斯顿大学获得博士学位，并回到哈佛大学担任博士后职位。他的博士生导师、菲尔兹奖得主曼朱尔·巴尔加瓦 (Manjul Bhargava) 也提到了同样的热情和才华，但他补充道，阿尔波格“写下他所做的新事物的速度很慢，部分原因是他总是在思考太多事情。”

paras.en: Bhargava also recalls a time when a family member on Long Island was ill and Levent offered to take leave from his job to move home and help. “I’ve never forgotten that gesture,” Bhargava says, calling Alpöge “a very kind and caring person.”
paras.zh: 巴尔加瓦还回忆起，有一次，长岛的一名家庭成员生病了，莱文特提出请假搬回家帮忙。 “我永远不会忘记那个举动，”巴尔加瓦说，并称阿尔波格是“一个非常善良和有爱心的人”。

paras.en: Yet Alpöge’s frenzied approach sometimes ruffled feathers in academia. In a pithy February 2025 Facebook post, he wrote that he’d solved a “Hilbert problem,” one of math’s big trophies. But two other mathematicians had already solved the problem. As of today, Alpöge still proudly lists the accolade on his website and X bio.
paras.zh: 然而，阿尔波格的疯狂做法有时会激怒学术界。在 2025 年 2 月的 Facebook 简洁帖子中，他写道，他解决了“希尔伯特问题”，这是数学界的一大奖杯。但另外两位数学家已经解决了这个问题。直到今天，Alpöge 仍然自豪地在他的网站和 X bio 上列出了这一荣誉。

paras.en: Alpöge’s departure to Anthropic in the summer of 2024 didn’t surprise anyone close to him. He frequently expressed frustrations with academia and its antiquated journal system, they say, and had become obsessed with AI from the moment he interacted with OpenAI’s GPT-4 in mid-2023.
paras.zh: Alpöge 于 2024 年夏天离开到 Anthropic，并没有让任何与他关系密切的人感到惊讶。他们说，他经常对学术界及其过时的期刊系统表示失望，从 2023 年中期与 OpenAI 的 GPT-4 互动那一刻起，他就开始沉迷于人工智能。

paras.en: He joined the company under a vague title, “member of technical staff.” Anthropic declined a request to give further information about his official work. Everyone with second-hand knowledge of the arrangement, however, insists he was not hired to do math.
paras.zh: 他以一个模糊的头衔加入公司：“技术人员”。 Anthropic 拒绝提供有关其官方工作的进一步信息的请求。然而，每个对这一安排有二手了解的人都坚称，他不是被雇来做数学的。

paras.en: But Anthropic employees are allowed to experiment with unreleased versions of Claude in their off time. “Give a math person access to a powerful LLM [large language model] with access to a lot of compute,” says M.I.T. mathematician Andrew Sutherland, “and they will eventually start asking it math questions, whether you want them to or not.”
paras.zh: 但 Anthropic 的员工可以在休息时间尝试未发行的 Claude 版本。麻省理工学院表示：“让数学人员能够接触到强大的 LLM（大型语言模型）并进行大量计算。”数学家安德鲁·萨瑟兰（Andrew Sutherland）表示，“无论你是否愿意，他们最终都会开始问它数学问题。”

paras.en: Alpöge first gained wider recognition on July 19, 2026, with a curt X post at 10:19 P.M. EDT announcing he had solved the Jacobian conjecture, one of math’s most famous problems. Another mathematician, Akhil Mathew of the University of Chicago, had thought that the conjecture might be within reach of cutting-edge AI models and had mentioned it in passing to Alpöge, who took the idea and ran with it.
paras.zh: Alpöge 于 2026 年 7 月 19 日晚上 10:19 发布了一条简短的 X 帖子，首次获得更广泛的认可。 EDT 宣布他解决了雅可比猜想，这是数学最著名的问题之一。另一位数学家、芝加哥大学的阿基尔·马修 (Akhil Mathew) 认为这个猜想可能可以用尖端人工智能模型实现，并在向 Alpöge 提及这一点时，Alpöge 接受了这个想法并付诸实践。

paras.en: This achievement was a turning point, the first really famous math problem AI solved—the sort of thing most people would’ve revealed in a long, explanatory manuscript submitted to a top math journal. To critics, Alpöge’s nonchalant post almost seemed to say, with a callous shrug, “Yup, AI is better than you now.” (Friends say Alpöge now regrets the approach he took, for which a number of prominent mathematicians have castigated him publicly and privately.)
paras.zh: 这一成就是一个转折点，是人工智能解决的第一个真正著名的数学问题——大多数人会在提交给顶级数学期刊的长篇解释性手稿中透露这一点。对于批评者来说，阿尔波格冷漠的帖子几乎像是在冷酷地耸耸肩说：“是的，人工智能现在比你更好。” （朋友们说，阿尔波格现在对他所采取的做法感到后悔，为此，许多著名数学家公开和私下严厉批评了他。）

paras.en: Over the following months, Alpöge repeated this pattern again and again. He’d think of a problem, either because he knew it from his own area of number theory or because another mathematician suggested it. He’d throw his allowance of tokens and an internal version of Claude at it and then inform a few trusted outside experts of what he found. If necessary, he’d iterate based on their feedback.
paras.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，Alpöge 一次又一次重复这种模式。他会想到一个问题，要么是因为他从自己的数论领域知道了这个问题，要么是因为另一位数学家提出了这个问题。他会投入自己的代币和克劳德的内部版本，然后将他的发现告知一些值得信赖的外部专家。如有必要，他会根据他们的反馈进行迭代。

paras.en: These breakthroughs—too numerous and esoteric to concisely list here—spanned a breathtaking range of mathematical topics, more than any single mathematician can productively work in. Of course, Alpöge didn’t need to understand each topic completely. He would act as a kind of liaison between his legions of Claude agents and his human collaborators.
paras.zh: 这些突破数量众多，深奥难懂，无法在这里一一列举，涵盖了令人惊叹的数学主题，超出了任何一个数学家所能有效完成的范围。当然，Alpöge 并不需要完全理解每个主题。他将充当他的克劳德特工军团和他的人类合作者之间的联络人。

paras.en: He’d give his agentic army a direction, often based on the human experts’ guidance, and they’d churn out thousands of pages of calculations, mostly in a math-slop dialect unreadable to any human. But the slop corresponded, in some impenetrable way, to actual mathematical truth. Alpöge’s task was to translate this output, with the help of yet another LLM, into readable math. He’s become a kind of LLM whisperer through this unconventional, somewhat aggravating process, which he calls “AI psychosis,” according to Ethan Sussman, a mathematician at Northwestern University.
paras.zh: 他会给他的代理军队一个方向，通常是根据人类专家的指导，他们会写出数千页的计算结果，大部分是用任何人都无法理解的数学方言。但这个斜率以某种难以理解的方式与实际的数学真理相对应。 Alpöge 的任务是在另一位法学硕士的帮助下将这一输出转化为可读的数学。西北大学数学家伊森·苏斯曼 (Ethan Sussman) 表示，通过这种非传统的、有些令人恼火的过程，他已经成为了一名法学硕士窃窃私语者，他称之为“人工智能精神病”。

paras.en: Still, Alpöge’s correspondents all remark on his shocking ability to grasp subjects far from his expertise—and on his unflagging resolve. “I think he really does understand all this math,” Armstrong says. “He’s like some kind of genius.”
paras.zh: 尽管如此，阿尔波格的记者们都称赞他掌握远离他专业知识的主题的惊人能力，以及他坚定不移的决心。 “我认为他确实理解所有这些数学，”阿姆斯特朗说。 “他就像某种天才。”

paras.en: “He is exceptionally broad,” Sussman agrees. While Sussman is usually the most intense person in his collaborations, “Levent is an order of magnitude more intense than I am,” he says. Alpöge “sets his sights on the goal, and he’s like, ‘I’ll sleep when this is done.’”
paras.zh: “他非常宽广，”萨斯曼表示同意。虽然萨斯曼通常是他合作中最热情的人，但“莱文特的热情比我高一个数量级，”他说。 Alpöge“将目光瞄准了目标，他说，‘完成后我就睡觉了。’”

paras.en: In fact, the issue of Alpöge’s sleep—or lack thereof—is something many of his recent collaborators have noticed with concern. His messages and check-ins, arriving at all hours, seem untethered from any circadian routine. “I don’t know when he’s sleeping,” several of his collaborators told me.
paras.zh: 事实上，阿尔波格的睡眠问题（或者说缺乏睡眠）是他最近的许多合作者都关心的问题。他的信息和报到信息随时都会到达，似乎不受任何昼夜节律的束缚。 “我不知道他什么时候睡觉，”他的几位合作者告诉我。

paras.en: What happened next was a crash. Just as Alpöge was nearing one of math’s loftiest summits, hoping to solve a “million-dollar” problem from the Clay Mathematics Institute’s Millennium Prize list—the highest-value math targets out there—Anthropic’s archrival, OpenAI, swooped in. Rumors had spread that Alpöge and N.Y.U. mathematician Tristan Buckmaster were about to solve the Navier-Stokes problem. Looking for a win, OpenAI’s math team threw colossal amounts of computing power at the problem over several days to get there first.
paras.zh: 接下来发生的是一场车祸。正当 Alpöge 接近数学最高峰之一，希望解决克莱数学研究所千年奖名单上的“百万美元”问题（最高价值的数学目标）时，Anthropic 的主要竞争对手 OpenAI 突然介入。数学家特里斯坦·巴克马斯特即将解决纳维-斯托克斯问题。为了寻求胜利，OpenAI 的数学团队在几天内投入了大量的计算能力来解决这个问题，以便首先实现这一目标。

paras.en: The media painted the controversy as a David versus Goliath narrative. Alpöge did his best to stay out of it and mostly avoided the uproar, while Buckmaster was cast as the human struck down by an iron-fisted tech juggernaut.
paras.zh: 媒体将这场争议描述为大卫与歌利亚的故事。阿尔波格尽最大努力置身事外，基本上避免了骚动，而巴克马斯特则扮演被铁腕科技巨头击倒的人类。

paras.en: A month later OpenAI followed up the Navier-Stokes blockbuster with more than 700 additional results. The proof dump fell upon a mathematical community already in turmoil. It also scooped a number of mathematicians’ progress on important problems, including collaborations with Alpöge that were underway. Any paranoia he already felt was now magnified, and he became increasingly withdrawn, convinced that leaks between the two companies were stealing his progress.
paras.zh: 一个月后，OpenAI 继 Navier-Stokes 的重磅成果之后又推出了 700 多项额外结果。证明转储落在了已经陷入混乱的数学界身上。它还报道了许多数学家在重要问题上的进展，包括正在进行的与 Alpöge 的合作。他已经感觉到的偏执现在被放大了，他变得越来越孤僻，确信两家公司之间的泄密正在窃取他的进步。

paras.en: The most impressive result in OpenAI’s dump, maybe the most impressive AI-powered result up until then, was a proof that made significant progress toward the Riemann hypothesis. This was Alpöge’s favorite problem, the one he’d harbored unspoken dreams of someday besting. Publicly, he posted on X to commend OpenAI’s team for its work. But the very same day, he started poking harder around the edges of the hypothesis with his internal version of Claude.
paras.zh: OpenAI 转储中最令人印象深刻的结果，也许是迄今为止最令人印象深刻的人工智能驱动的结果，是在黎曼假设方面取得重大进展的证明。这是阿尔波格最喜欢的问题，他心中暗暗梦想有一天能打败这个问题。他公开在 X 上发帖赞扬 OpenAI 团队的工作。但就在同一天，他开始用他内心版本的克劳德更努力地探索这个假设的边缘。

paras.en: On October 14 Armstrong sat down on a bench in Alpöge’s hotel lobby in Aspen, Colo.
paras.zh: 10 月 14 日，阿姆斯特朗坐在科罗拉多州阿斯彭 Alpöge 酒店大堂的长凳上。

paras.en: He’d messaged Alpöge, whom he knew was in Aspen for the same secret “AIxMath” conference, because he hadn’t seen him at any of the events. Alpöge said he’d been hiding out in his hotel room and suggested they go for a walk.
paras.zh: 他给 Alpöge 发了消息，他知道 Alpöge 正在阿斯彭参加同一个秘密“AIxMath”会议，因为他在任何活动中都没有见过他。阿尔波格说，他一直躲在酒店房间里，建议他们去散步。

paras.en: The two had only spoken once before, at an N.Y.U. lunch in July. Armstrong was showing Alpöge’s Jacobian conjecture X post on his phone to colleagues around the table. He couldn’t figure out why they were giggling until the stranger with a bowl cut sitting next to him turned and said with a smile, “That was me.”
paras.zh: 两人之前只说过一次话，是在纽约大学。七月的午餐。阿姆斯特朗正在手机上向桌旁的同事展示 Alpöge 的雅可比猜想 X 帖子。他不明白他们为什么咯咯地笑，直到坐在他旁边的那个留着碗形头发的陌生人转过身来，笑着说道：“那是我。”

paras.en: When Alpöge finally emerged in the lobby in October, Armstrong barely recognized him. His hair was shaggier, his facial hair had grown out, and he was cloaked in a baggy hoodie. “He looked ‘like a hobo,’ in his own words,” Armstrong recalls. “He didn’t want to be seen by anyone.”
paras.zh: 当十月份阿尔波格最终出现在大厅时，阿姆斯特朗几乎认不出他了。他的头发更加蓬乱，面部毛发也长出来了，他穿着一件宽松的连帽衫。 “用他自己的话来说，他看起来‘像个流浪汉’，”阿姆斯特朗回忆道。 “他不想被任何人看见。”

paras.en: They strolled through Aspen’s quiet streets for two hours, talking about the Navier-Stokes drama and the powerful, AI-fueled forces that were forging their collective future. This time Alpöge offered no goofy quips, and his frustration was clear. “He’s a very intense person—he’s very moody,” Armstrong says. “He thinks that OpenAI is the evil empire, and he just wants to throw as much sand in their gears as he can.”
paras.zh: 他们在阿斯彭安静的街道上漫步了两个小时，谈论着纳维-斯托克斯的戏剧以及正在塑造他们共同未来的强大的、由人工智能驱动的力量。这次阿尔波格没有提出任何愚蠢的俏皮话，他的挫败感显而易见。 “他是一个非常热情的人——他非常喜怒无常，”阿姆斯特朗说。 “他认为 OpenAI 是邪恶帝国，他只是想尽可能多地往他们的齿轮里扔沙子。”

paras.en: Alpöge doesn’t seem to think Anthropic is perfect either, but he’s glad it exists. When Armstrong complained of math’s fate being in the hands of just two companies, Alpöge replied, “It could be worse. At least there’s not just one.”
paras.zh: Alpöge 似乎也不认为 Anthropic 是完美的，但他很高兴它的存在。当阿姆斯特朗抱怨数学的命运只掌握在两家公司手中时，阿尔波格回答道：“情况可能会更糟。至少不只有一家公司。”

paras.en: Alpöge hadn’t expressed such animosity toward his corporate rivals before this year’s headline-making events, according to everyone I spoke with. But OpenAI’s actions this year, rife with PR-heavy claims and rampant scooping of mathematicians (Alpöge most of all), seems to have made an enemy of him.
paras.zh: 据我采访过的每个人都说，在今年的头条新闻之前，阿尔波格从未对他的企业竞争对手表达过如此敌意。但 OpenAI 今年的行动充满了公关宣传和对数学家（尤其是 Alpöge）的猖獗挖角，似乎已经与他为敌了。

paras.en: Alpöge himself now has no shortage of enemies. In the aftermath of his Riemann proof, he wrote on X, he’s received death threats. And many mathematicians are frustrated with the official narrative, promoted by Alpöge and Anthropic alike, that his math work is merely a “hobby” entirely divorced from his day job—especially when he’s using internal models and resources.
paras.zh: 阿尔波格本人现在也不乏敌人。他在 X 上写道，黎曼证明完成后，他收到了死亡威胁。许多数学家对 Alpöge 和 Anthropic 等公司宣扬的官方说法感到沮丧，即他的数学工作只是一种“爱好”，完全脱离了他的日常工作——尤其是当他使用内部模型和资源时。

paras.en: Three mathematicians uploaded a preprint last week that provides a rare insight into those resources. Alpöge had shared with them the LLM output from one of his summer breakthroughs. They used it to estimate that the discovery—which was several times less ambitious than many of Alpöge’s other projects—cost up to $4 million worth of computing resources. An Anthropic representative declined to comment on the estimate. Whatever Anthropic’s “allowance” for Alpöge is, it’s not an especially cheap one. (Similarly, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman recently acknowledged that costs for his company’s math efforts reached more than $100 million.) For reference, in 2026 the National Science Foundation, the largest U.S. funder of math research, invested about $200 million in the field.
paras.zh: 三位数学家上周上传了一份预印本，提供了对这些资源的罕见见解。 Alpöge 与他们分享了他夏季突破之一的法学硕士成果。他们用它来估计这一发现（比 Alpöge 的许多其他项目要小几倍）花费了价值 400 万美元的计算资源。 Anthropic 的一位代表拒绝对这一估计发表评论。无论 Anthropic 对 Alpöge 的“补贴”是多少，它都不是特别便宜的。 （同样，OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 最近承认，其公司数学研究的成本超过 1 亿美元。）作为参考，2026 年，美国最大的数学研究资助者国家科学基金会在该领域投资了约 2 亿美元。

paras.en: “Anthropic should release how much this costs. How many tens of millions of dollars are in their budget to solve math problems?” says N.Y.U. mathematician Nestor Guillen. In mid-October, Guillen notes, Anthropic and OpenAI each committed $5 million in funding and resources to a joint initiative with the Simons Foundation to help mathematicians understand recent AI breakthroughs. “Would they agree to increase that money to match what they give an employee working on a ‘weekend hobby?’” he asks.
paras.zh: “Anthropic应该公布这需要多少钱。他们的预算中有多少数千万美元用于解决数学问题？”纽约大学说数学家内斯特·吉兰。 Guillen 指出，10 月中旬，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 各自承诺为与西蒙斯基金会的一项联合计划提供 500 万美元的资金和资源，以帮助数学家了解最近的人工智能突破。 “他们会同意增加这笔钱，以匹配他们给予从事‘周末爱好’的员工的钱吗？”他问道。

paras.en: After their afternoon walk in Aspen, Armstrong and Alpöge parted ways, heading back to their respective hotel rooms, where each had a number of agents churning on their current math problems. What Alpöge was working on, he did not disclose.
paras.zh: 下午在阿斯彭散步后，阿姆斯特朗和阿尔波格分道扬镳，回到各自的酒店房间，房间里都有一些特工在忙着解决当前的数学问题。 Alpöge 正在做什么，他没有透露。

paras.en: Alpöge and Claude’s successes on Riemann happened in spurts throughout October and November. In the early hours of November 16, they did the impossible. That was when Alpöge wrote to Anthropic’s CEO Dario Amodei, who asked him to save the announcement until after the company’s initial public offering (IPO) that Friday.
paras.zh: 阿尔波格和克劳德在黎曼问题上的成功在整个 10 月和 11 月期间都取得了突飞猛进的进展。 11 月 16 日凌晨，他们完成了不可能的任务。当时 Alpöge 写信给 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代 (Dario Amodei)，后者要求他将这一公告保留到该公司周五首次公开募股 (IPO) 之后。

paras.en: That day Alpöge visited Princeton University, where he told Bhargava and mathematician Peter Sarnak what he’d accomplished, swearing them to secrecy and asking their advice. “It was surreal,” Sarnak says. “He was in a pretty excited state.” Alpöge spent the rest of the week holed up in Buckmaster’s N.Y.U. office, their old war room during the Navier-Stokes drama, where they now strategized the release of the Riemann proof.
paras.zh: 那天，阿尔波格访问了普林斯顿大学，在那里他告诉巴尔加瓦和数学家彼得·萨纳克他的成就，让他们发誓保密并征求他们的建议。 “这太超现实了，”萨纳克说。 “他当时的状态非常兴奋。”这周剩下的时间里，阿尔波格都躲在巴克马斯特的纽约大学里。办公室，他们在纳维-斯托克斯戏剧中的旧作战室，现在他们在那里制定了发布黎曼证明的策略。

paras.en: Drained but exhilarated, they wrapped up their work early on Friday morning and walked to the touristy Caffe Reggio on MacDougal Street, the only place nearby that was still serving decent coffee past 2 A.M.
paras.zh: 周五一早，他们就结束了工作，虽然筋疲力尽，但仍兴奋不已，步行前往位于麦克杜格尔街 (MacDougal Street) 的旅游胜地雷吉奥咖啡馆 (Caffe Reggio)，这是附近唯一一家在凌晨 2 点过后仍然提供优质咖啡的地方。

paras.en: Love him or hate him, Alpöge has given mathematicians a human face to represent the AI revolution, to project their feelings onto as their world is turned upside down. In his statement about the Riemann proof, Alpöge gave ample praise to Claude—“Claude flew, and danced, and sparkled near that finish line.” But he also highlighted his own agency. “It was my secret in my student days that my plans were for this problem,” he wrote. He used a machine to beat everyone, yes, but he remains a key ingredient. The story he has spun is one of triumphant partnership, portending a bright future for math—a modern retelling of the same “lone genius” story math has always been obsessed with, updated for the AI era.
paras.zh: 不管你爱他还是恨他，Alpöge 为数学家们提供了一张人性化的面孔来代表人工智能革命，让他们在世界发生翻天覆地的变化时投射出他们的感受。在关于黎曼证明的声明中，阿尔波格对克劳德给予了充分的赞扬——“克劳德在终点线附近飞翔、跳舞、闪闪发光。”但他也强调了自己的机构。 “在我学生时代，我的计划就是解决这个问题，这是我的秘密，”他写道。是的，他用机器打败了所有人，但他仍然是一个关键因素。他编造的故事是一个胜利的合作伙伴关系，预示着数学的光明未来——这是对数学一直痴迷的同一个“孤独天才”故事的现代重述，并为人工智能时代进行了更新。

paras.en: Whether he’s a visionary genius or a corporate face, his process and his foibles are a stark glimpse into math’s new, supercharged future—AI psychosis included. Riemann being solved won’t cure cancer or stop global warming. It probably won’t change your life in any noticeable way. But it marks a turning point nonetheless, one whose import will only be fully known to our future selves.
paras.zh: 无论他是一位有远见的天才还是一位企业界人士，他的过程和他的缺点都是数学新的、充满活力的未来的鲜明一瞥——包括人工智能精神病。解决黎曼问题并不能治愈癌症或阻止全球变暖。它可能不会以任何明显的方式改变你的生活。但这仍然标志着一个转折点，其重要性只有我们未来的自己才能完全了解。

paras.en: The upload finished shortly after 8 A.M. on November 20. Alpöge texted Buckmaster the link to his website and instructed him to pass it to Armstrong. “Levent and I always joked, ‘If we ever need anything leaked, we’ll just give it to Scott,’” Buckmaster says. Armstrong posted it to X immediately. It was done.
paras.zh: 上午 8 点刚过，上传就完成了。 11 月 20 日，阿尔波格向巴克马斯特发送了他网站的链接，并指示他将其传递给阿姆斯特朗。 “莱文特和我总是开玩笑说，‘如果我们需要泄露任何东西，我们就把它交给斯科特，’”巴克马斯特说。阿姆斯特朗立即将其发布到 X。事情完成了。

paras.en: But what if there was a bug? Alpöge realized he hadn’t had time to compile the code on his own machine before uploading it. Could something have gotten garbled in the process? People around the world would download his code, and it would crash, making them doubt his claim.
paras.zh: 但如果出现错误怎么办？ Alpöge 意识到他在上传代码之前没有时间在自己的机器上编译代码。在此过程中是否会出现乱码？世界各地的人们都会下载他的代码，但它会崩溃，让他们怀疑他的说法。

paras.en: It was done—the files were already online; the world already informed. But he had to know. Bleary-eyed, he started up his compiler. He could sleep once he knew he’d won.
paras.zh: 完成了——文件已经在线了；世界已经获悉。但他必须知道。他睡眼惺忪地启动了编译器。一旦他知道自己赢了，他就可以睡觉了。

paras.en: *Editor’s Note (11/25/26): This sentence was edited after posting to correct the description of Levent Alpöge’s record in the “pig’s trough” challenge.
paras.zh: *编者注（11/25/26）：这句话是在发帖后编辑的，以更正 Levent Alpöge 在“猪槽”挑战中的记录描述。

articles.title: Do you need to be worried about flying for Thanksgiving this year? We asked the experts

paras.en: The busiest travel days of the year are here, less than two weeks after a historic ground stop, numerous tech and airline outages and swirling questions over what could possibly go wrong now. Ahead of Thanksgiving, we asked experts the question at the top of our family group chats: Will it be safe to fly?
paras.zh: 一年中最繁忙的旅行日即将到来，距离历史性的地面停留不到两周，科技和航空公司出现大量中断，人们对现在可能出现问题的问题产生了疑问。感恩节前夕，我们在家庭群聊中向专家询问了这个问题：飞行安全吗？

paras.en: The short answer is yes, says Arnold Barnett, a statistician at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, who studies aviation. So far this year, roughly 800 million passengers have flown on commercial planes run by U.S. airlines, he says—and each one landed safely.
paras.zh: 麻省理工学院研究航空的统计学家阿诺德·巴尼特说，简短的答案是肯定的。他说，今年到目前为止，大约有 8 亿乘客乘坐美国航空公司运营的商用飞机出行，而且每一位乘客都安全着陆。

paras.en: That includes the recent ground stop on November 13, which the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said was caused by a problem with equipment during repair works at a remote facility that led to widespread communications problems. No air traffic control centers fully lost contact, Barnett points out, and all planes that were in the air during the ground stop landed safely.
paras.zh: 其中包括最近 11 月 13 日的地面停飞，美国联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 表示，此次停飞是由于偏远设施维修期间出现设备问题，导致广泛的通信问题。巴尼特指出，没有空中交通管制中心完全失去联系，并且在地面停留期间在空中的所有飞机都安全着陆。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “Our air traffic controllers and safety professionals are working around the clock to keep Americans moving during what is expected to be the busiest Thanksgiving travel week in 16 years,” said FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford in a statement posted online.
paras.zh: 美国联邦航空局局长布莱恩·贝德福德 (Bryan Bedford) 在网上发布的一份声明中表示：“我们的空中交通管制员和安全专业人员正在全天候工作，以确保美国人在预计将是 16 年来最繁忙的感恩节旅行周期间保持出行。”

paras.en: According to data from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), which tracks air incidents, 2026 has seen fewer aviation accidents through October than any previous year at that point—1,216 compared with 1,267 in 2025 and more than 13,00 in each previous year, except 2020, which had fewer accidents in the same time frame. Of the accidents recorded through October this year, 244 accidents were fatal and 972 were nonfatal, compared with 240 and 1,027, respectively, in 2025.
paras.zh: 根据跟踪航空事故的美国国家运输安全委员会 (NTSB) 的数据，2026 年 10 月份的航空事故数量比以往任何一年都要少 — — 1,216 起，而 2025 年为 1,267 起，之前每年都超过 13,00 起，但 2020 年除外，2020 年同期事故数量较少。截至今年 10 月记录的事故中，死亡事故为 244 起，非致命事故为 972 起，而 2025 年分别为 240 起和 1,027 起。

paras.en: Indeed, January 2025 saw the first fatal U.S. commercial plane crash in 16 years, when an American Airlines flight collided with a military helicopter over Washington, D.C. The NTSB, which advises the FAA, currently has dozens of open recommendations to increase safety following such aviation incidents.
paras.zh: 事实上，2025 年 1 月，美国航空公司的一架飞机在华盛顿特区上空与一架军用直升机相撞，发生了 16 年来第一起致命的美国商用飞机失事事件。为 FAA 提供建议的 NTSB 目前已提出数十项公开建议，以在发生此类航空事故后提高安全性。

paras.en: David Woods, a U.S. safety systems researcher, says that he trusts commercial planes to carry his grandchildren safely this holiday season—but that this doesn’t mean our aviation systems don’t warrant a critical look moving forward. Woods says he is concerned about so-called reactive safety, or the practice of prioritizing technological innovation and then only adding safety measures once accidents have already happened. The country’s aviation infrastructure is aging, and as it’s updated, officials appear to be prioritizing technological advances such as artificial intelligence over safety needs, he says.
paras.zh: 美国安全系统研究员戴维·伍兹 (David Woods) 表示，他相信商用飞机能够在这个假期安全地载着他的孙子们，但这并不意味着我们的航空系统不值得对未来进行严格的审视。伍兹表示，他担心所谓的反应安全，即优先考虑技术创新，然后在事故发生后才添加安全措施的做法。他说，该国的航空基础设施正在老化，随着基础设施的更新，官员们似乎将人工智能等技术进步置于安全需求之上。

paras.en: “We’re worried on two fronts,” Woods says. “One is that we’re starting to backslide a little on the safety advances, and two is that the changing technology and scale of systems is creating new risks that we’re not seeing and anticipating.”
paras.zh: “我们担心两个方面，”伍兹说。 “一是我们在安全进步方面开始出现一些倒退，二是不断变化的技术和系统规模正在创造我们没有看到和预料到的新风险。”

paras.en: Najmedin Meshkati, an engineering professor at the University of Southern California, who served on an expert panel for the FAA following a fatal crash of a Boeing 737 MAX plane in Indonesia in 2018 and another in Ethiopia in 2019, points out that many aviation accidents happen on the runway—not in the sky. He says that issues with technology and human factors, such as understaffed air traffic control centers, can impact safety. Hundreds of FAA workers were laid off in “Department of Government Efficiency” (U.S. DOGE Service)–related cuts in 2025. The Department of Transportation has tried to bolster hiring for air traffic controllers since then; in response to a request for comment from Scientific American, the department said that no air traffic controllers were cut by DOGE.
paras.zh: 南加州大学工程学教授纳吉梅丁·梅斯卡蒂 (Najmedin Meshkati) 曾在 2018 年印度尼西亚一架波音 737 MAX 飞机和 2019 年埃塞俄比亚一架波音 737 MAX 飞机发生致命坠机事件后担任美国联邦航空局专家小组成员。他指出，许多航空事故都发生在跑道上，而不是天空中。他表示，技术和人为因素问题（例如空中交通管制中心人手不足）可能会影响安全。 2025 年，数百名 FAA 员工因“政府效率部”（美国 DOGE 服务）相关裁员而被解雇。此后，交通部一直试图加强空中交通管制员的招聘；在回应《科学美国人》的置评请求时，该部门表示，没有任何空中交通管制员被 DOGE 解雇。

paras.en: Still, “the recent accidents, close calls and equipment failures are not isolated events,” Meshkati says. “They are symptoms of how people, organizations and technology interact, and fail to interact, in an overstretched system.”
paras.zh: 尽管如此，“最近发生的事故、险情和设备故障并不是孤立事件，”梅斯卡蒂说。 “它们是人、组织和技术在过度拉伸的系统中如何交互以及无法交互的症状。”

articles.title: The hidden math behind this paradoxical Black Friday sale strategy

paras.en: “Found a lower price elsewhere? We’ll match it.” When big-box stores make these promises they sound like they’re on your side. Best Buy, Home Depot and Lowe’s will match prices from Amazon, Walmart and more than a dozen other retailers. Some go even further. Australian hardware giant Bunnings promises to beat any competitor’s lower price by a full 10 percent. In the U.S. Home Depot, Lowe’s and Sears once gave similar offers.
paras.zh: “在其他地方找到更低的价格？我们会匹配的。”当大型商店做出这些承诺时，他们听起来就像是站在你这边的。百思买、家得宝和劳氏将与亚马逊、沃尔玛和其他十几家零售商的价格相匹配。有些甚至更进一步。澳大利亚硬件巨头 Bunnings 承诺将比任何竞争对手的价格低整整 10%。在美国家得宝(Home Depot)，劳氏(Lowe's)和西尔斯(Sears)也曾给出过类似的优惠。

paras.en: But game theory suggests these guarantees are less generous than they appear. In fact, they can paradoxically keep prices high. One telling clue is that many retailers switch off their competitor price matching around Black Friday and Cyber Monday, the most competitive shopping stretch of the year.
paras.zh: 但博弈论表明，这些保证并不像看上去那么慷慨。事实上，他们可能会自相矛盾地保持高价格。一个明显的线索是，许多零售商在黑色星期五和网络星期一（一年中竞争最激烈的购物时段）前后停止了竞争对手的价格匹配。

paras.en: In 1883 French mathematician Joseph Bertrand published a scathing review of a book that offered one of the first mathematical models of economic competition. In that model, rival firms decide how much to produce, and the market settles on what the price is. Bertrand objected by saying that real sellers compete by setting and adapting prices, not production quantities. In just a few sentences, he sketched an argument that still informs how economists think about price competition.
paras.zh: 1883 年，法国数学家约瑟夫·贝特朗 (Joseph Bertrand) 对一本书发表了严厉的评论，该书提供了最早的经济竞争数学模型之一。在该模型中，竞争对手公司决定生产多少，而市场则决定价格。伯特兰反对说，真正的卖家通过设定和调整价格而不是产量来竞争。他仅用几句话就勾勒出一个论点，至今仍然影响着经济学家如何看待价格竞争。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Suppose a retailer called Store A sells a television that costs $500 to buy directly from the manufacturer. If it were the only store selling TVs, it would charge the price that earns it the most money, with no competition to incentivize a lower price." Perhaps $900 marks the store’s sweet spot: enough shoppers will pay that much, but if the cost were any higher, too many would decide the TV wasn’t worth it.
paras.zh: 假设一家名为 A 店的零售商出售一台直接从制造商处购买的电视机，售价为 500 美元。如果它是唯一一家销售电视的商店，它会收取最赚钱的价格，没有竞争来激励更低的价格。”也许 900 美元标志着商店的最佳定价：足够多的购物者愿意支付这么多钱，但如果成本更高，太多人会认为电视不值得。

paras.en: Now introduce a competitor, Store B, carrying the same TV, which also costs it $500. If both stores charge $900, customers might feel indifferent about where to purchase a TV, and the stores will roughly split the sales. But if Store A drops its price to $899, then every bargain hunter will go its way, and Store A will reap all of the profits. In the face of this, Store B drops its price to $898, and so on in a race to the bottom.
paras.zh: 现在介绍一下竞争对手，Store B，也有同样的电视，价格也为 500 美元。如果两家商店都收取 900 美元，顾客可能会觉得去哪里购买电视并不重要，商店就会大致平分销售额。但如果 A 店把价格降到 899 美元，那么每个逢低买进的人就会各走各的，A 店就会获得所有利润。面对这种情况，B 店将价格降至 898 美元，以此类推，竞相降价。

paras.en: Left unchecked, this undercutting would stop only at $500, with neither store earning a dime on the sale. Real prices rarely fall quite that far. Stores differ in location and brand loyalty, shoppers don’t check every ad, and stores eventually learn that if they cut prices once, they’ll have to do so again and again to stay competitive.
paras.zh: 如果不加以控制，这种降价只会止于 500 美元，而且两家商店都不会在促销中赚到一分钱。实际价格很少会下跌那么远。商店的位置和品牌忠诚度各不相同，购物者不会检查每条广告，商店最终会了解到，如果他们降价一次，他们就必须一次又一次地降价以保持竞争力。

paras.en: Yet Bertrand’s core insight still holds: sellers compete via price setting, and the threat of being undercut prevents stores from charging whatever they want. Both stores in the hypothetical scenario would be better off holding at $900, but they don’t. That’s because each worries the other will lower the price, and any agreement to hold the line would amount to price-fixing collusion, which is illegal. It’s a version of the prisoner’s dilemma that happens to benefit consumers. Both sellers fare better when they collude, but they can’t trust each other, so instead they compete. That’s why economists worry about monopolies. A store with no rivals to fear can charge the profit-maximizing $900 and make shoppers either pay above their comfort zone or skip the product altogether.
paras.zh: 然而，伯特兰的核心见解仍然成立：卖家通过定价进行竞争，而被压价的威胁会阻止商店随意收取费用。在假设的情况下，两家商店最好保持 900 美元的价格，但他们没有。这是因为双方都担心对方会降低价格，而任何保留底线的协议都将构成串通定价，这是非法的。这是囚徒困境的一个版本，但恰好对消费者有利。当两个卖家串通时，他们的表现会更好，但他们不能互相信任，所以他们会竞争。这就是经济学家担心垄断的原因。一家没有竞争对手的商店可以收取 900 美元的利润最大化费用，让购物者要么支付超出他们舒适范围的费用，要么完全跳过该产品。

paras.en: Now suppose Store A hangs a sign saying, “We’ll match any competitor’s price.” When Store B considers cutting to $899, the calculation changes. Without Store A’s price-matching offer, Store B’s cut would poach every bargain hunter. Now those shoppers can show Store B’s price at Store A and pay $899 there, so Store B wins no new customers and earns less on the ones it already had. If Store A goes further and promises to beat lower prices from rivals, as some stores do, then Store B’s price cut would actually backfire, sending Store B’s customers to Store A for a better deal. When these guarantees are in place, cutting prices no longer pays, so both stores stay at $900. Without any backroom dealings, the two stores have landed on the price that a monopoly would choose—and the ploy that secured this reads like generosity.
paras.zh: 现在假设 A 商店挂了一个牌子，上面写着：“我们将与任何竞争对手的价格相匹配。”当商店 B 考虑削减至 899 美元时，计算结果发生了变化。如果没有 A 店的价格匹配优惠，B 店的折扣就会挖走每一个讨价还价的人。现在，这些购物者可以在 A 店展示 B 店的价格，并在那里支付 899 美元，因此 B 店没有赢得新客户，并且在现有客户上赚取的收入也减少了。如果 A 店更进一步，承诺以更低的价格打败竞争对手，就像一些商店所做的那样，那么 B 店的降价实际上会适得其反，将 B 店的顾客带到 A 店以获得更优惠的价格。当这些保证到位后，降价就不再划算了，所以两家商店的价格都维持在 900 美元。在没有任何幕后交易的情况下，这两家商店已经确定了垄断者会选择的价格——而确保这一点的策略看起来像是慷慨的。

paras.en: Three things about price matching are worth noticing. First, only one store needs the guarantee—Store A’s promise to match competitors' prices protects Store B’s high price as much as its own. Second, a guarantee that functions as intended almost never gets used. In the idealized model nobody undercuts, so no shopper ever has a lower price to bring to the register. Third, the sign looks like it’s addressed to consumers, but it’s actually a message to rival stores.
paras.zh: 关于价格匹配的三件事值得注意。首先，只有一家商店需要保证——商店 A 承诺与竞争对手的价格保持一致，这既保护了商店 B 的高价格，也保护了商店 B 的高价格。其次，保证功能按预期运行几乎永远不会被使用。在理想化的模型中，没有人会降价，因此购物者不会以更低的价格进入收银台。第三，这个标牌看起来像是针对消费者的，但实际上是向竞争对手商店传达的信息。

paras.en: Shoppers rarely see it this way. A 2003 paper in the Journal of Consumer Psychology tellingly entitled “Failing to Suspect Collusion in Price-Matching Guarantees” concluded that people tend to interpret price-matching offers as a signal that prices are already low, not as a way of keeping them high.
paras.zh: 购物者很少这样看待。 2003 年，《消费者心理学杂志》上发表的一篇题​​为“未能怀疑价格匹配保证中的共谋”的论文引人注目，其结论是，人们倾向于将价格匹配优惠视为价格已经很低的信号，而不是保持价格较高的一种方式。

paras.en: Whether real stores behave in accordance with Bertrand’s model is an empirical question, and the evidence says they often do, under the right conditions. A 1991 study tracked supermarket prices before and after stores adopted price-matching guarantees and found that price matching caused higher prices overall. More recently economist Ran Zhuo examined what happened when big-box chains began promising to match Amazon. Theory predicted that Amazon would stop undercutting—and that’s exactly what Zhuo’s 2017 paper reports. Amazon’s prices rose by roughly six percentage points after the guarantees took effect, according to the paper.
paras.zh: 真实商店的行为是否符合伯特兰模型是一个经验问题，证据表明，在适当的条件下，它们经常这样做。 1991 年的一项研究跟踪了商店采用价格匹配保证前后的超市价格，发现价格匹配导致总体价格上涨。最近，经济学家卓然研究了当大型连锁店开始承诺与亚马逊竞争时会发生什么。 Theory 预测亚马逊将停止低价竞争——而这正是 Zhuo 在 2017 年的论文中所报道的。据该报报道，担保生效后，亚马逊的价格上涨了约六个百分点。

paras.en: Of course, real markets get messy and rarely play out exactly as described in economics textbooks. The effect is strongest under particular conditions: a few big rivals selling identical products where price matches are easy for customers to claim. Economists Morten Hviid and Greg Shaffer showed in 1999 that price-matching offers lose their power when shoppers have to jump through hoops to claim them. Rivals know that few customers will bother, so the threat meant to deter undercutting loses credibility.
paras.zh: 当然，真实的市场会变得混乱，很少会完全按照经济学教科书描述的那样发展。这种效应在特定条件下最为强烈：几个大竞争对手销售相同的产品，而客户很容易声称价格匹配。经济学家 Morten Hviid 和 Greg Shaffer 在 1999 年指出，当购物者必须克服重重困难才能获得价格匹配优惠时，价格匹配优惠就会失去效力。竞争对手知道很少有顾客会打扰，因此旨在阻止低价竞争的威胁失去了可信度。

paras.en: Retailers pitch price-matching guarantees as a promise to make sure you never overpay. But if that were their purpose, then the guarantees would matter most during sales events like Black Friday, when prices swing wildly. Instead that’s exactly when many retailers switch them off. On a normal day a price-matching guarantee discourages rivals from undercutting, so the offer costs stores very little. It works as a threat that rarely gets called. Doorbuster events such as Black Friday and Cyber Monday are all about steep cuts, however, and those cuts will come no matter what, so price matching won’t deter stores from making them. In this setting, price matching wouldn’t operate as a low-cost threat but rather a costly mistake, with stores beholden to every rival’s lowest price. Retailers tend not to explain why they suspend price matching during sales events, yet the timing is telling.
paras.zh: 零售商将价格匹配保证作为确保您永远不会多付钱的承诺。但如果这是他们的目的，那么在黑色星期五等销售活动期间，当价格剧烈波动时，保证就变得最重要。相反，这正是许多零售商关闭它们的时候。在正常情况下，价格匹配保证会阻止竞争对手降价，因此商店的报价成本非常低。它就像一种威胁，但很少被召唤。然而，诸如“黑色星期五”和“网络星期一”之类的重大活动都是大幅降价，而且无论如何，降价都会发生，因此价格匹配不会阻止商店进行降价。在这种情况下，价格匹配不会成为一种低成本威胁，而是一个代价高昂的错误，商店必须遵守每个竞争对手的最低价格。零售商往往不会解释为什么他们在销售活动期间暂停价格匹配，但时机很能说明问题。

paras.en: None of this means you should skip a price match when you find one. If a guarantee saves you money, use it. Just read the offer for what it is: a signal to the store down the street that undercutting won’t pay.
paras.zh: 这些并不意味着您在找到价格匹配时应该跳过价格匹配。如果担保可以为您省钱，请使用它。只需阅读报价内容即可：这是向街上的商店发出的信号，表明降价是不值得的。

articles.title: What helps land recover after fire? This ecologist looks to the past
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: In an increasingly fire-prone western North America, Jennifer Grenz, an ecologist and member of the Lytton First Nation, looks at fire with a holistic eye. She considers her work with landscapes recovering from catastrophic wildfire to be “deliberately unfocused,” spanning soil microbial ecology, restoration ecology, invasion biology and historical biology.
paras.zh: 在越来越容易发生火灾的北美西部，生态学家兼利顿原住民成员詹妮弗·格伦茨 (Jennifer Grenz) 以整体的眼光看待火灾。她认为她对从灾难性野火中恢复的景观的研究“故意没有重点”，涵盖土壤微生物生态学、恢复生态学、入侵生物学和历史生物学。

paras.en: Grenz analyzes historical ecological records, like how Indigenous people have shaped and cared for ecosystems over time, to paint a comprehensive picture. “I’m interested in how those histories leave ecological legacies and hints of the stewardship of the past,” says Grenz, who leads the Indigenous Ecology Lab at the University of British Columbia in Canada. “What changed on the land that made it more vulnerable?”
paras.zh: 格伦茨分析了历史生态记录，例如土著人民如何随着时间的推移塑造和照顾生态系统，以描绘出一幅全面的图景。 “我对这些历史如何留下生态遗产和过去管理的暗示感兴趣，”加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚大学土著生态实验室的负责人格伦茨说。 “这片土地发生了什么变化，使其变得更加脆弱？”

paras.en: Grenz spends time with many kinds of specialists, such as archaeologists, anthropologists and Indigenous elders who provide oral histories.
paras.zh: 格伦茨与许多类型的专家共度时光，例如考古学家、人类学家和提供口述历史的土著长者。

paras.en: Moving forward, her lab will examine ecology below ground, including soil, microbial communities and root networks. The goal is to understand the role of underground ecology in critical topics like carbon sequestration, climate change, biodiversity and sustainable management.
paras.zh: 展望未来，她的实验室将研究地下生态，包括土壤、微生物群落和根系网络。目标是了解地下生态在碳封存、气候变化、生物多样性和可持续管理等关键主题中的作用。

paras.en: “My motivation is in our interior Salish Territories in the southern interior of British Columbia, where my ancestors rest and where my people are,” Grenz says. “The responsibility I feel to them and to our Tmícw, which means our lands, [is] to not take us back to the past, but to show that we have the deep knowledge to help us move forward.”
paras.zh: “我的动机是在不列颠哥伦比亚省南部内陆的萨利什​​领地，那里是我的祖先安息的地方，也是我的人民居住的地方，”格伦茨说。 “我对他们和我们的 Tmícw（这意味着我们的土地）感到的责任是不要让我们回到过去，而是要表明我们拥有深厚的知识来帮助我们前进。”

articles.title: This scientist proves which problems computers can’t solve quickly
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: Dor Minzer remembers sitting in an undergraduate computation class at Tel Aviv University. He was intrigued by his professor and soon found himself pulled into a new world: the mystifying intersection of math and computation, first laid out by Alan Turing during World War II. Working with the professor, Minzer became deeply interested in the limitations of what computers can and can’t do.
paras.zh: 多尔·明泽 (Dor Minzer) 记得参加特拉维夫大学的本科生计算课程。他对教授很感兴趣，很快就发现自己被带入了一个新世界：数学与计算的神秘交叉点，这是阿兰·图灵在二战期间首次提出的。与教授一起工作，明泽对计算机能做什么和不能做什么的局限性产生了浓厚的兴趣。

paras.en: “My part is actually to prove not only do I not know how to do it, but I can prove that it’s impossible,” Minzer says. “You have to really be curious.”
paras.zh: “我的职责实际上是证明我不仅不知道如何做到这一点，而且我可以证明这是不可能的，”明泽说。 “你必须真正感到好奇。”

paras.en: Minzer’s hard work has paid off. In 2018, he proved a theoretical computer science problem called the 2-to-2 games conjecture. It asks whether computers can efficiently distinguish games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where almost none can be satisfied, when the rules have a strict structure.
paras.zh: 明泽的努力得到了回报。 2018年，他证明了一个名为“2对2博弈猜想”的计算机科学理论问题。它询问当规则具有严格的结构时，计算机是否能够有效区分几乎所有规则都可以满足的游戏和几乎没有规则可以满足的游戏。

paras.en: In September, Minzer and his two graduate students at MIT posted a 95-page milestone paper on the unique games conjecture, which builds off the 2-to-2 conjecture. The paper wasn’t quite ready, but they published to get ahead of a press release from OpenAI, describing its proof for the same problem, slated for only days later. It’s a situation that many mathematicians have found themselves in this year as AI companies flood the field with findings at lightning speed.
paras.zh: 9 月份，明泽和他在麻省理工学院的两名研究生发表了一篇长达 95 页的里程碑式论文，内容涉及独特的游戏猜想，该猜想建立在 2-2 猜想的基础上。这篇论文还没有完全准备好，但他们在 OpenAI 发布新闻稿之前发表，描述了同一问题的证明，该新闻稿定于几天后发布。今年，随着人工智能公司以闪电般的速度将研究成果涌入该领域，许多数学家都遇到了这种情况。

paras.en: Minzer says it’s critical to remember that math, and all the research and contemplation behind it, is very human. “It’s a human activity,” he says. “Research is sort of a living organism, a living body.”
paras.zh: 明泽说，重要的是要记住，数学及其背后的所有研究和思考都是非常人性化的。 “这是一项人类活动，”他说。 “研究是一个活的有机体，一个活的身体。”

paras.en: Minzer teaches his own students now. Some days, he talks to his class and gets the sense that nobody is paying attention. But other days, he gets a few students that participate. They have ideas, they’re excited, and they remind him of his own days as a graduate student.
paras.zh: 明泽现在教自己的学生。有时，他在班上讲话时，会感觉到没有人注意。但其他时候，他也会有一些学生参加。他们有想法，他们很兴奋，他们让他想起自己作为研究生的日子。

paras.en: “I feel like now I feel like I’m passing the torch,” he says. “Before you have a Ph.D. adviser, you’re like a new person in a dark room. There are infinite places to go. Your Ph.D. adviser is the person that holds your hand and says, ‘Okay, let’s walk here.’”
paras.zh: “我觉得现在我正在传递火炬，”他说。 “在没有博士生导师之前，你就像一个黑屋子里的新人。有无数个地方可以去。你的博士生导师就是那个握着你的手说：‘好吧，我们走到这里’的人。”
